v: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius,[^1] the word of the LORD[^2] came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet:[^3]
בַּחֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הַשְּׁמִינִ֔י בִּשְׁנַ֥ת שְׁתַּ֖יִם לְדָרְיָ֑וֶשׁ הָיָ֣ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־זְכַרְיָה֙ בֶּן־בֶּ֣רֶכְיָ֔ה בֶּן־עִדּ֥וֹ הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃
The LORD was very angry with your ancestors.[^4]
קָצַ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה עַל־אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם קָֽצֶף׃
So say to them: This is what the LORD of Armies[^5] says: Return to me, declares the LORD of Armies,[^6] and I will return to you, says the LORD of Armies.[^7]
וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֗ם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת שׁ֣וּבוּ אֵלַ֔י נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְאָשׁ֣וּב אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

Do not be like your ancestors, to whom the earlier prophets[^8] proclaimed, "This is what the LORD of Armies says: Turn back from your evil ways and your evil deeds." But they did not listen or pay attention to me, declares the LORD.

אַל־תִּהְי֣וּ כַאֲבֹֽתֵיכֶ֡ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר קָרְאֽוּ־אֲלֵיהֶם֩ הַנְּבִיאִ֨ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֜ים לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת שׁ֤וּבוּ נָא֙ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֣ם הָרָעִ֔ים *ומעליליכם **וּמַֽעֲלְלֵיכֶ֖ם הָֽרָעִ֑ים וְלֹ֥א שָׁמְע֛וּ וְלֹֽא־הִקְשִׁ֥יבוּ אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
Your ancestors, where are they now? And the prophets, do they live forever?
אֲבֽוֹתֵיכֶ֖ם אַיֵּה־הֵ֑ם וְהַ֨נְּבִאִ֔ים הַלְעוֹלָ֖ם יִֽחְיֽוּ׃

But my words and my decrees, which I commanded my servants the prophets, did they not overtake your ancestors? Then they repented and said, "The LORD of Armies has dealt with us as he planned to do, according to our ways and our deeds."

אַ֣ךְ ׀ דְּבָרַ֣י וְחֻקַּ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר צִוִּ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־עֲבָדַ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים הֲל֥וֹא הִשִּׂ֖יגוּ אֲבֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וַיָּשׁ֣וּבוּ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר זָמַ֜ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָ֔נוּ כִּדְרָכֵ֙ינוּ֙ וּכְמַ֣עֲלָלֵ֔ינוּ כֵּ֖ן עָשָׂ֥ה אִתָּֽנוּ׃ ס
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius,[^9] the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet.[^10]

בְּיוֹם֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֜ה לְעַשְׁתֵּֽי־עָשָׂ֥ר חֹ֙דֶשׁ֙ הוּא־חֹ֣דֶשׁ שְׁבָ֔ט בִּשְׁנַ֥ת שְׁתַּ֖יִם לְדָרְיָ֑וֶשׁ הָיָ֣ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֗ה אֶל־זְכַרְיָה֙ בֶּן־בֶּ֣רֶכְיָ֔הוּ בֶּן־עִדּ֥וֹא הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃
I saw in the night, and there was a man riding on a red horse! He was standing among the myrtle trees in the ravine,[^11] and behind him were red, sorrel[^12] and white horses.
רָאִ֣יתִי ׀ הַלַּ֗יְלָה וְהִנֵּה־אִישׁ֙ רֹכֵב֙ עַל־ס֣וּס אָדֹ֔ם וְה֣וּא עֹמֵ֔ד בֵּ֥ין הַהֲדַסִּ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמְּצֻלָ֑ה וְאַחֲרָיו֙ סוּסִ֣ים אֲדֻמִּ֔ים שְׂרֻקִּ֖ים וּלְבָנִֽים׃
I asked, "What are these, my lord?"[^13] The angel who was speaking with me[^14] said to me, "I will show you what they are."
וָאֹמַ֖ר מָה־אֵ֣לֶּה אֲדֹנִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י הַמַּלְאָךְ֙ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֔י אֲנִ֥י אַרְאֶ֖ךָּ מָה־הֵ֥מָּה אֵֽלֶּה׃
Then the man who was standing among the myrtle trees answered, "These are the ones the LORD has sent to patrol the earth."[^15]
וַיַּ֗עַן הָאִ֛ישׁ הָעֹמֵ֥ד בֵּין־הַהַדַסִּ֖ים וַיֹּאמַ֑ר אֵ֚לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁלַ֣ח יְהוָ֔ה לְהִתְהַלֵּ֖ךְ בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
They answered the angel of the LORD who was standing among the myrtle trees,[^16] "We have patrolled the earth, and the whole earth is still and at rest."[^17]
וַֽיַּעֲנ֞וּ אֶת־מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה הָֽעֹמֵד֙ בֵּ֣ין הַהֲדַסִּ֔ים וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ הִתְהַלַּ֣כְנוּ בָאָ֑רֶץ וְהִנֵּ֥ה כָל־הָאָ֖רֶץ יֹשֶׁ֥בֶת וְשֹׁקָֽטֶת׃
Then the angel of the LORD said, "LORD of Armies, how long will you withhold your compassion from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, with which you have been angry these seventy years?"[^18]
וַיַּ֣עַן מַלְאַךְ־יְהוָה֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת עַד־מָתַ֗י אַתָּה֙ לֹֽא־תְרַחֵ֣ם אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר זָעַ֔מְתָּה זֶ֖ה שִׁבְעִ֥ים שָׁנָֽה׃
The LORD answered the angel who was speaking with me with kind and comforting words.
וַיַּ֣עַן יְהוָ֗ה אֶת־הַמַּלְאָ֛ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֥ר בִּ֖י דְּבָרִ֣ים טוֹבִ֑ים דְּבָרִ֖ים נִחֻמִֽים׃
Then the angel who was speaking with me said to me, "Proclaim: 'This is what the LORD of Armies says: I am very jealous[^19] for Jerusalem and for Zion,
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י הַמַּלְאָךְ֙ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֔י קְרָ֣א לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת קִנֵּ֧אתִי לִירוּשָׁלַ֛͏ִם וּלְצִיּ֖וֹן קִנְאָ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃
and I am very angry with the nations that are at ease. For I was only a little angry, but they made the disaster worse.[^20]
וְקֶ֤צֶף גָּדוֹל֙ אֲנִ֣י קֹצֵ֔ף עַל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם הַשַּֽׁאֲנַנִּ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִי֙ קָצַ֣פְתִּי מְּעָ֔ט וְהֵ֖מָּה עָזְר֥וּ לְרָעָֽה׃

Therefore this is what the LORD says: I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion. My house will be rebuilt in it, declares the LORD of Armies, and a measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.'[^21]
לָכֵ֞ן כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה שַׁ֤בְתִּי לִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ בְּֽרַחֲמִ֔ים בֵּיתִי֙ יִבָּ֣נֶה בָּ֔הּ נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת *וקוה **וְקָ֥ו יִנָּטֶ֖ה עַל־יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Proclaim again: 'This is what the LORD of Armies says: My cities will again overflow with prosperity, and the LORD will again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem.'"[^22]
ע֣וֹד ׀ קְרָ֣א לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת ע֛וֹד תְּפוּצֶ֥ינָה עָרַ֖י מִטּ֑וֹב וְנִחַ֨ם יְהוָ֥ה עוֹד֙ אֶת־צִיּ֔וֹן וּבָחַ֥ר ע֖וֹד בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃ ס

n.1: October or November 520 BC, two months after Haggai's first message (Haggai 1:1). Darius I was king of Persia.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: *Zechariah* means "The LORD remembers". He prophesied together with Haggai (Ezra 5:1; 6:14), and was probably of the priestly family of Iddo, which returned from exile with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 12:4, 16). Ezra calls him "son of Iddo", perhaps meaning "grandson".
n.4: Literally "The LORD was angry with your ancestors with anger".
n.5: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. The title is used more than fifty times in Zechariah.
n.6: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH tseva'ot*, "the declaration of the LORD of Armies", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement.
n.7: Malachi 3:7 repeats the words "Return to me, and I will return to you".
n.8: The prophets before the exile, such as Jeremiah (Jeremiah 25:4–5; 35:15).
n.9: 15 February 519 BC. *Shebat* is the Babylonian name of the month, used after the exile.
n.10: From here to 6:15 Zechariah tells of eight visions he saw in one night, each explained to him by an angel. Many of their details are uncertain.
n.11: Hebrew *metsulah*, "deep place", perhaps a valley near Jerusalem, or the deep waters at the edge of the world.
n.12: Hebrew *seruqqim*, a color of uncertain meaning, perhaps reddish brown or speckled.
n.13: Hebrew *adoni*, a polite form of address, not the title of God.
n.14: Hebrew *mal'akh*, "messenger, angel". This angel explains the visions throughout chapters 1–6.
n.15: Literally "to walk about in the earth", like the patrols and messengers of the Persian king. Compare Job 1:7.
n.16: The angel of the LORD is apparently the man of verses 8 and 10.
n.17: The Persian empire was at peace after Darius had put down the revolts at the start of his reign, but Jerusalem still lay in ruins.
n.18: Jeremiah had foretold seventy years of exile (Jeremiah 25:11–12; 29:10). The temple had been destroyed in 587 or 586 BC, nearly seventy years before.
n.19: Literally "I am jealous with great jealousy", the passion of the LORD for his people. Compare 8:2.
n.21: A line for measuring the ground before building (Jeremiah 31:38–39).
n.22: In most English Bibles chapter 1 has verses 18–21, which are 2:1–4 in the Hebrew.

v: Then I looked up and saw four horns.[^1]
וָאֶשָּׂ֥א אֶת־עֵינַ֖י וָאֵ֑רֶא וְהִנֵּ֖ה אַרְבַּ֥ע קְרָנֽוֹת׃
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these?" He said to me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem."
וָאֹמַ֗ר אֶל־הַמַּלְאָ֛ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֥ר בִּ֖י מָה־אֵ֑לֶּה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י אֵ֤לֶּה הַקְּרָנוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר זֵר֣וּ אֶת־יְהוּדָ֔ה אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וִירוּשָׁלָֽם׃ ס
Then the LORD[^2] showed me four craftsmen.[^3]
וַיַּרְאֵ֣נִי יְהוָ֔ה אַרְבָּעָ֖ה חָרָשִֽׁים׃

I asked, "What are these coming to do?" He said, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, so that no one could lift up his head. But these craftsmen have come to terrify them, to throw down the horns of the nations that lifted up their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."

וָאֹמַ֕ר מָ֛ה אֵ֥לֶּה בָאִ֖ים לַֽעֲשׂ֑וֹת וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאמֹ֗ר אֵ֣לֶּה הַקְּרָנ֞וֹת אֲשֶׁר־זֵ֣רוּ אֶת־יְהוּדָ֗ה כְּפִי־אִישׁ֙ לֹא־נָשָׂ֣א רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וַיָּבֹ֤אוּ אֵ֙לֶּה֙ לְהַחֲרִ֣יד אֹתָ֔ם לְיַדּ֞וֹת אֶת־קַרְנ֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֗ם הַנֹּשְׂאִ֥ים קֶ֛רֶן אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָ֖ה לְזָרוֹתָֽהּ׃ ס
Then I looked up and saw a man with a measuring line in his hand.
וָאֶשָּׂ֥א עֵינַ֛י וָאֵ֖רֶא וְהִנֵּה־אִ֑ישׁ וּבְיָד֖וֹ חֶ֥בֶל מִדָּֽה׃
I asked, "Where are you going?" He said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide it is and how long."
וָאֹמַ֕ר אָ֖נָה אַתָּ֣ה הֹלֵ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י לָמֹד֙ אֶת־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לִרְא֥וֹת כַּמָּֽה־רָחְבָּ֖הּ וְכַמָּ֥ה אָרְכָּֽהּ׃
Then the angel who was speaking with me came forward, and another angel came out to meet him.
וְהִנֵּ֗ה הַמַּלְאָ֛ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֥ר בִּ֖י יֹצֵ֑א וּמַלְאָ֣ךְ אַחֵ֔ר יֹצֵ֖א לִקְרָאתֽוֹ׃
He said to him, "Run, tell that young man:[^4] 'Jerusalem will be inhabited like open villages without walls,[^5] because of the great number of people and animals in it.
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔ו רֻ֗ץ דַּבֵּ֛ר אֶל־הַנַּ֥עַר הַלָּ֖ז לֵאמֹ֑ר פְּרָזוֹת֙ תֵּשֵׁ֣ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם מֵרֹ֥ב אָדָ֛ם וּבְהֵמָ֖ה בְּתוֹכָֽהּ׃
And I myself will be a wall of fire around it, declares the LORD,[^6] and I will be the glory within it.'"
וַאֲנִ֤י אֶֽהְיֶה־לָּהּ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה ח֥וֹמַת אֵ֖שׁ סָבִ֑יב וּלְכָב֖וֹד אֶֽהְיֶ֥ה בְתוֹכָֽהּ׃ פ
Come! Come![^7] Flee from the land of the north, declares the LORD, for I have scattered you like the four winds of the heavens,[^8] declares the LORD.
ה֣וֹי ה֗וֹי וְנֻ֛סוּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ צָפ֖וֹן נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֠י כְּאַרְבַּ֞ע רוּח֧וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֛יִם פֵּרַ֥שְׂתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
Come, Zion! Escape, you who live with Daughter Babylon!
ה֥וֹי צִיּ֖וֹן הִמָּלְטִ֑י יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בַּת־בָּבֶֽל׃ ס
For this is what the LORD of Armies[^9] says, he who sent me after glory[^10] to the nations that plundered you: Whoever touches you touches the pupil of his eye.[^11]
כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָמַר֮ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֒ אַחַ֣ר כָּב֔וֹד שְׁלָחַ֕נִי אֶל־הַגּוֹיִ֖ם הַשֹּׁלְלִ֣ים אֶתְכֶ֑ם כִּ֚י הַנֹּגֵ֣עַ בָּכֶ֔ם נֹגֵ֖עַ בְּבָבַ֥ת עֵינֽוֹ׃
For look, I am going to wave my hand against them,[^12] and they will become plunder for those who served them. Then you will know that the LORD of Armies has sent me.
כִּ֠י הִנְנִ֨י מֵנִ֤יף אֶת־יָדִי֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וְהָי֥וּ שָׁלָ֖ל לְעַבְדֵיהֶ֑ם וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחָֽנִי׃ ס
Sing and rejoice, Daughter Zion,[^13] for look, I am coming, and I will live among you,[^14] declares the LORD.
רָנִּ֥י וְשִׂמְחִ֖י בַּת־צִיּ֑וֹן כִּ֧י הִנְנִי־בָ֛א וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֥י בְתוֹכֵ֖ךְ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃
Many nations will join themselves to the LORD on that day and become my people. I will live among you, and you will know that the LORD of Armies has sent me to you.
וְנִלְווּ֩ גוֹיִ֨ם רַבִּ֤ים אֶל־יְהוָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְהָ֥יוּ לִ֖י לְעָ֑ם וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֣י בְתוֹכֵ֔ךְ וְיָדַ֕עַתְּ כִּי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֵלָֽיִךְ׃
The LORD will take possession of Judah as his portion in the holy land,[^15] and he will again choose Jerusalem.
וְנָחַ֨ל יְהוָ֤ה אֶת־יְהוּדָה֙ חֶלְק֔וֹ עַ֖ל אַדְמַ֣ת הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ וּבָחַ֥ר ע֖וֹד בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
Be silent, all humankind,[^16] before the LORD, for he has roused himself from his holy dwelling.
הַ֥ס כָּל־בָּשָׂ֖ר מִפְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כִּ֥י נֵע֖וֹר מִמְּע֥וֹן קָדְשֽׁוֹ׃ ס

n.1: Verses 1–4 are 1:18–21 in most English Bibles, and verses 5–17 are 2:1–13. Horns are a picture of strength, here of the nations that conquered Israel and Judah.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *charashim*, skilled workers in metal, wood or stone, who would cut the horns down.
n.4: Probably the man with the measuring line (verse 5), or Zechariah himself.
n.5: Hebrew *perazot*, "open country, unwalled villages". The city will be too large for walls.
n.6: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. Also in verses 10 and 14.
n.7: Hebrew *hoy*, usually "Woe to" (Amos 5:18). Here, and in verse 11, it is a call for attention. Verses 10–17 call the exiles home from Babylon, the "land of the north", from which invaders came to Israel.
n.8: The Septuagint reads "I will gather you from the four winds of the heavens".
n.9: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verses 13 and 15.
n.10: The meaning is uncertain. Literally "after glory he sent me". Perhaps "for the sake of his glory", or "after the Glory sent me". The speaker may be the prophet or the angel.
n.11: Literally "the gate of his eye", the pupil, which is guarded with great care (Deuteronomy 32:10). This is one of the *tiqqune sopherim*, the rabbinic "corrections of the scribes": the tradition says that the text once read "my eye" and was changed out of reverence for God.
n.13: A poetic name for Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman. Compare Zephaniah 3:14.
n.14: Hebrew *shakhan*, the verb used of the LORD's dwelling among his people in the tabernacle (Exodus 25:8). Also in verse 15.
n.15: The only place in the Bible where the land is called "holy".

v: Then he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD,[^1] and the Accuser[^2] standing at his right hand to accuse him.
וַיַּרְאֵ֗נִי אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁ֙עַ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֔וֹל עֹמֵ֕ד לִפְנֵ֖י מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֑ה וְהַשָּׂטָ֛ן עֹמֵ֥ד עַל־יְמִינ֖וֹ לְשִׂטְנֽוֹ׃
The LORD said to the Accuser, "The LORD rebuke you, Accuser! The LORD, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebuke you![^3] Is not this man a burning stick snatched from the fire?"[^4]
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־הַשָּׂטָ֗ן יִגְעַ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה בְּךָ֙ הַשָּׂטָ֔ן וְיִגְעַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ בְּךָ֔ הַבֹּחֵ֖ר בִּירֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם הֲל֧וֹא זֶ֦ה א֖וּד מֻצָּ֥ל מֵאֵֽשׁ׃
Now Joshua was dressed in filthy clothes[^5] as he stood before the angel.
וִיהוֹשֻׁ֕עַ הָיָ֥ה לָבֻ֖שׁ בְּגָדִ֣ים צוֹאִ֑ים וְעֹמֵ֖ד לִפְנֵ֥י הַמַּלְאָֽךְ׃
The angel said to those who were standing before him, "Take the filthy clothes off him." And to Joshua he said, "See, I have taken your guilt away from you, and I will clothe you in festal robes."
וַיַּ֣עַן וַיֹּ֗אמֶר אֶל־הָעֹמְדִ֤ים לְפָנָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הָסִ֛ירוּ הַבְּגָדִ֥ים הַצֹּאִ֖ים מֵעָלָ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו רְאֵ֨ה הֶעֱבַ֤רְתִּי מֵעָלֶ֙יךָ֙ עֲוֺנֶ֔ךָ וְהַלְבֵּ֥שׁ אֹתְךָ֖ מַחֲלָצֽוֹת׃
Then I said, "Let them put a clean turban[^6] on his head." So they put a clean turban on his head and clothed him with garments, while the angel of the LORD stood by.
וָאֹמַ֕ר יָשִׂ֛ימוּ צָנִ֥יף טָה֖וֹר עַל־רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיָּשִׂימוּ֩ הַצָּנִ֨יף הַטָּה֜וֹר עַל־רֹאשׁ֗וֹ וַיַּלְבִּשֻׁ֙הוּ֙ בְּגָדִ֔ים וּמַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה עֹמֵֽד׃
Then the angel of the LORD solemnly charged Joshua:
וַיָּ֙עַד֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה בִּיהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ לֵאמֹֽר׃

"This is what the LORD of Armies[^7] says: If you walk in my ways and keep my charge,[^8] then you will govern my house and have charge of my courts, and I will give you the right to come and go[^9] among these who are standing here.

כֹּה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת אִם־בִּדְרָכַ֤י תֵּלֵךְ֙ וְאִ֣ם אֶת־מִשְׁמַרְתִּ֣י תִשְׁמֹ֔ר וְגַם־אַתָּה֙ תָּדִ֣ין אֶת־בֵּיתִ֔י וְגַ֖ם תִּשְׁמֹ֣ר אֶת־חֲצֵרָ֑י וְנָתַתִּ֤י לְךָ֙ מַהְלְכִ֔ים בֵּ֥ין הָעֹמְדִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
Listen, Joshua the high priest, you and your colleagues who sit before you, for they are men who are a sign:[^10] I am going to bring my servant the Branch.[^11]
שְֽׁמַֽע־נָ֞א יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ ׀ הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֗וֹל אַתָּה֙ וְרֵעֶ֙יךָ֙ הַיֹּשְׁבִ֣ים לְפָנֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־אַנְשֵׁ֥י מוֹפֵ֖ת הֵ֑מָּה כִּֽי־הִנְנִ֥י מֵבִ֛יא אֶת־עַבְדִּ֖י צֶֽמַח׃

For look, the stone that I have set before Joshua: on one stone there are seven eyes.[^12] I am going to engrave an inscription on it, declares the LORD of Armies,[^13] and I will remove the guilt of this land in a single day.

כִּ֣י ׀ הִנֵּ֣ה הָאֶ֗בֶן אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָתַ֙תִּי֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ עַל־אֶ֥בֶן אַחַ֖ת שִׁבְעָ֣ה עֵינָ֑יִם הִנְנִ֧י מְפַתֵּ֣חַ פִּתֻּחָ֗הּ נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּמַשְׁתִּ֛י אֶת־עֲוֺ֥ן הָאָֽרֶץ־הַהִ֖יא בְּי֥וֹם אֶחָֽד׃
On that day, declares the LORD of Armies, each of you will invite his neighbor to sit under his vine and under his fig tree."[^14]
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת תִּקְרְא֖וּ אִ֣ישׁ לְרֵעֵ֑הוּ אֶל־תַּ֥חַת גֶּ֖פֶן וְאֶל־תַּ֥חַת תְּאֵנָֽה׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *ha-satan*, "the adversary, the accuser", with the article: a title rather than a name. Traditionally "Satan". *To accuse him* is *le-sitno*, from the same root. The accuser stood at the right hand of the accused in a court (Psalm 109:6). Also in verse 2.
n.3: Jude 9 echoes these words: "The Lord rebuke you."
n.4: Joshua and his people have been rescued from the fire of the exile (compare Amos 4:11).
n.5: Hebrew *tso'im*, "soiled with excrement", the filthiest of words. Also in verse 4.
n.6: Hebrew *tsanif*, a word related to *mitsnefet*, the turban of the high priest (Exodus 28:4, 36–39).
n.7: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.8: Hebrew *mishmeret*, the duties of the priests in the sanctuary (Leviticus 8:35; Numbers 3:7).
n.9: Literally "places to walk", perhaps access to the council of heaven (compare Jeremiah 23:18, 22).
n.10: Hebrew *mofet*, "sign, portent", a sign of things to come (Isaiah 8:18).
n.11: Hebrew *tsemach*, "sprout, growth", a title of a coming king of David's line (Jeremiah 23:5; 33:15; Zechariah 6:12). The Aramaic Targum reads "my servant the anointed one (Messiah)".
n.12: The meaning of the stone is uncertain. It may be a stone for the temple, or a gem for the high priest's turban, which was engraved "Holy to the LORD" (Exodus 28:36–38). *Eyes* may mean "facets" or "springs". Compare 4:10.
n.13: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH tseva'ot*, "the declaration of the LORD of Armies", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. Also in verse 10.
n.14: A picture of peace and safety (1 Kings 5:5, 4:25 in most English Bibles; Micah 4:4).

v: Then the angel who was speaking with me came back and woke me, as someone is woken from sleep.
וַיָּ֕שָׁב הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֑י וַיְעִירֵ֕נִי כְּאִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יֵע֥וֹר מִשְּׁנָתֽוֹ׃
He asked me, "What do you see?" I said,[^1] "I see a lampstand all of gold, with a bowl on top of it. It has seven lamps on it, with seven spouts for each of the lamps on top of it.[^2]

וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י מָ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה רֹאֶ֑ה *ויאמר **וָאֹמַ֡ר רָאִ֣יתִי ׀ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מְנוֹרַת֩ זָהָ֨ב כֻּלָּ֜הּ וְגֻלָּ֣הּ עַל־רֹאשָׁ֗הּ וְשִׁבְעָ֤ה נֵרֹתֶ֙יהָ֙ עָלֶ֔יהָ שִׁבְעָ֤ה וְשִׁבְעָה֙ מֽוּצָק֔וֹת לַנֵּר֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל־רֹאשָֽׁהּ׃
There are two olive trees beside it, one on the right of the bowl and the other on its left."
וּשְׁנַ֥יִם זֵיתִ֖ים עָלֶ֑יהָ אֶחָד֙ מִימִ֣ין הַגֻּלָּ֔ה וְאֶחָ֖ד עַל־שְׂמֹאלָֽהּ׃
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these, my lord?"
וָאַ֙עַן֙ וָֽאֹמַ֔ר אֶל־הַמַּלְאָ֛ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֥ר בִּ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר מָה־אֵ֖לֶּה אֲדֹנִֽי׃
The angel who was speaking with me answered, "Do you not know what these are?" I said, "No, my lord."
וַ֠יַּעַן הַמַּלְאָ֞ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֥ר בִּי֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י הֲל֥וֹא יָדַ֖עְתָּ מָה־הֵ֣מָּה אֵ֑לֶּה וָאֹמַ֖ר לֹ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי׃
Then he said to me, "This is the word of the LORD[^3] to Zerubbabel: Not by might and not by power, but by my Spirit,[^4] says the LORD of Armies.[^5]
וַיַּ֜עַן וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר זֶ֚ה דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר לֹ֤א בְחַ֙יִל֙ וְלֹ֣א בְכֹ֔חַ כִּ֣י אִם־בְּרוּחִ֔י אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
What are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become a plain. He will bring out the top stone[^6] amid shouts of 'Grace, grace to it!'"[^7]
מִֽי־אַתָּ֧ה הַֽר־הַגָּד֛וֹל לִפְנֵ֥י זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל לְמִישֹׁ֑ר וְהוֹצִיא֙ אֶת־הָאֶ֣בֶן הָרֹאשָׁ֔ה תְּשֻׁא֕וֹת חֵ֥ן חֵ֖ן לָֽהּ׃ פ
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will complete it. Then you will know that the LORD of Armies has sent me to you.
יְדֵ֣י זְרֻבָּבֶ֗ל יִסְּד֛וּ הַבַּ֥יִת הַזֶּ֖ה וְיָדָ֣יו תְּבַצַּ֑עְנָה וְיָ֣דַעְתָּ֔ כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחַ֥נִי אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃
For who has despised the day of small things? They will rejoice when they see the plumb line[^8] in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven are the eyes of the LORD, which range over the whole earth.[^9]
כִּ֣י מִ֣י בַז֮ לְי֣וֹם קְטַנּוֹת֒ וְשָׂמְח֗וּ וְרָא֞וּ אֶת־הָאֶ֧בֶן הַבְּדִ֛יל בְּיַ֥ד זְרֻבָּבֶ֖ל שִׁבְעָה־אֵ֑לֶּה עֵינֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה הֵ֥מָּה מְ[t]שׁוֹטְטִ֖ים בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Then I asked him, "What are these two olive trees on the right and on the left of the lampstand?"
וָאַ֖עַן וָאֹמַ֣ר אֵלָ֑יו מַה־שְּׁנֵ֤י הַזֵּיתִים֙ הָאֵ֔לֶה עַל־יְמִ֥ין הַמְּנוֹרָ֖ה וְעַל־שְׂמֹאולָֽהּ׃
And a second time I asked him, "What are these two branches[^10] of the olive trees, beside the two gold pipes, which pour out the golden oil[^11] from themselves?"
וָאַ֣עַן שֵׁנִ֔ית וָאֹמַ֖ר אֵלָ֑יו מַה־שְׁתֵּ֞י שִׁבֲּלֵ֣י הַזֵּיתִ֗ים אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּיַ֗ד שְׁנֵי֙ צַנְתְּר֣וֹת הַזָּהָ֔ב הַֽמְרִיקִ֥ים מֵעֲלֵיהֶ֖ם הַזָּהָֽב׃
He said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" I said, "No, my lord."
וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲל֥וֹא יָדַ֖עְתָּ מָה־אֵ֑לֶּה וָאֹמַ֖ר לֹ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי׃
Then he said, "These are the two anointed ones[^12] who stand by the Lord of the whole earth."
וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אֵ֖לֶּה שְׁנֵ֣י בְנֵֽי־הַיִּצְהָ֑ר הָעֹמְדִ֖ים עַל־אֲד֥וֹן כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

n.1: The Hebrew text is written "he said" but read "I said".
n.2: Or "and seven spouts for the seven lamps". Literally "seven and seven spouts for the lamps". The lampstand recalls the seven-branched lampstand of the tabernacle (Exodus 25:31–40), but its form is different and uncertain.
n.3: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.4: Hebrew *ruach*, "spirit, wind, breath". *Might* is *chayil*, which can also mean "army".
n.5: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verse 9.
n.6: Hebrew *ha-even ha-roshah*, "the head stone", perhaps the last stone set at the top of the building, or a stone from the first temple laid at the start of the work.
n.8: Literally "the stone of tin", probably the weight of a plumb line, used to see that a wall is straight. Or "the chosen stone".
n.9: The seven eyes are the seven lamps of verse 2, and this answers Zechariah's question in verse 4. Verses 6–10 may join an oracle about Zerubbabel to the explanation of the vision. Compare 3:9; 2 Chronicles 16:9; Revelation 5:6.
n.10: Literally "ears of grain", perhaps clusters of olives or branches heavy with fruit.
n.12: Literally "the two sons of the fresh oil". The word is not *mashiach*, "anointed", but the picture is of anointing with oil. They are probably Zerubbabel, of the royal line, and Joshua the high priest. Revelation 11:4 speaks of two witnesses as "the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth".

v: Again I looked up, and I saw a flying scroll.
וָאָשׁ֕וּב וָאֶשָּׂ֥א עֵינַ֖י וָֽאֶרְאֶ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֖ה מְגִלָּ֥ה עָפָֽה׃
He asked me, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a flying scroll, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide."[^1]
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י מָ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה רֹאֶ֑ה וָאֹמַ֗ר אֲנִ֤י רֹאֶה֙ מְגִלָּ֣ה עָפָ֔ה אָרְכָּהּ֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים בָּֽאַמָּ֔ה וְרָחְבָּ֖הּ עֶ֥שֶׂר בָּאַמָּֽה׃

He said to me, "This is the curse that is going out over the whole land. For according to what is written on one side, every thief will be swept away,[^2] and according to what is written on the other side, everyone who swears falsely[^3] will be swept away.
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י זֹ֚את הָֽאָלָ֔ה הַיּוֹצֵ֖את עַל־פְּנֵ֣י כָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ כִּ֣י כָל־הַגֹּנֵ֗ב מִזֶּה֙ כָּמ֣וֹהָ נִקָּ֔ה וְכָל־הַ֨נִּשְׁבָּ֔ע מִזֶּ֖ה כָּמ֥וֹהָ נִקָּֽה׃

I will send it out, declares the LORD of Armies,[^4] and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by my name. It will stay inside his house and destroy it, both its timbers and its stones."[^5]
הוֹצֵאתִ֗יהָ נְאֻם֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּבָ֙אָה֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַגַּנָּ֔ב וְאֶל־בֵּ֛ית הַנִּשְׁבָּ֥ע בִּשְׁמִ֖י לַשָּׁ֑קֶר וְלָ֙נֶה֙ בְּת֣וֹךְ בֵּית֔וֹ וְכִלַּ֖תּוּ וְאֶת־עֵצָ֥יו וְאֶת־אֲבָנָֽיו׃
Then the angel who was speaking with me came forward and said to me, "Look up and see what this is that is going out."
וַיֵּצֵ֕א הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י שָׂ֣א נָ֤א עֵינֶ֙יךָ֙ וּרְאֵ֔ה מָ֖ה הַיּוֹצֵ֥את הַזֹּֽאת׃
I asked, "What is it?" He said, "This is the ephah basket[^6] that is going out." And he said, "This is their iniquity[^7] in all the land."
וָאֹמַ֖ר מַה־הִ֑יא וַיֹּ֗אמֶר זֹ֤את הָֽאֵיפָה֙ הַיּוֹצֵ֔את וַיֹּ֕אמֶר זֹ֥את עֵינָ֖ם בְּכָל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
Then a round cover of lead[^8] was lifted, and there was a woman sitting inside the basket.
וְהִנֵּ֛ה כִּכַּ֥ר עֹפֶ֖רֶת נִשֵּׂ֑את וְזֹאת֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֔ת יוֹשֶׁ֖בֶת בְּת֥וֹךְ הָאֵיפָֽה׃
He said, "This is Wickedness." He thrust her back into the basket and pushed the lead weight down over its mouth.
וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ זֹ֣את הָרִשְׁעָ֔ה וַיַּשְׁלֵ֥ךְ אֹתָ֖הּ אֶל־תּ֣וֹךְ הָֽאֵיפָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁלֵ֛ךְ אֶת־אֶ֥בֶן הָעֹפֶ֖רֶת אֶל־פִּֽיהָ׃ ס
Then I looked up and saw two women coming out, with the wind[^9] in their wings. They had wings like the wings of a stork, and they lifted up the basket between earth and heaven.

וָאֶשָּׂ֨א עֵינַ֜י וָאֵ֗רֶא וְהִנֵּה֩ שְׁתַּ֨יִם נָשִׁ֤ים יֽוֹצְאוֹת֙ וְר֣וּחַ בְּכַנְפֵיהֶ֔ם וְלָהֵ֥נָּה כְנָפַ֖יִם כְּכַנְפֵ֣י הַחֲסִידָ֑ה וַתִּשֶּׂ֙אנָה֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֵיפָ֔ה בֵּ֥ין הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבֵ֥ין הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "Where are they taking the basket?"
וָאֹמַ֕ר אֶל־הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֑י אָ֛נָה הֵ֥מָּה מֽוֹלִכ֖וֹת אֶת־הָאֵיפָֽה׃
He said to me, "To build a house[^10] for it in the land of Shinar.[^11] When the house is ready, the basket will be set down there on its stand."
וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י לִבְנֽוֹת־לָ֥הֿ בַ֖יִת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ שִׁנְעָ֑ר וְהוּכַ֛ן וְהֻנִּ֥יחָה שָּׁ֖ם עַל־מְכֻנָתָֽהּ׃ ס

n.1: A cubit was about 18 inches (45 cm), so the scroll was about 30 feet (9 m) long and 15 feet (4.5 m) wide, the size of the porch of Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6:3).
n.2: Or "has gone unpunished". The Hebrew verb *niqqah* can mean "be cleaned out" or "be held innocent". Also later in the verse.
n.3: Literally "everyone who swears". *Falsely* is supplied from verse 4. Stealing and swearing falsely by the LORD's name break two of the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:7, 15).
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. *Declares the LORD* is Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement.
n.5: Compare the house struck by mold in Leviticus 14:45.
n.6: Literally "the ephah", a dry measure of about 22 liters (two-thirds of a bushel), here a basket or barrel of that size. Also in verses 7–11.
n.7: Hebrew *einam*, "their eye", perhaps "their appearance". The Septuagint and the Syriac read *avonam*, "their iniquity", which differs by one letter.
n.8: Literally "a talent of lead", a round, flat piece of lead of a set weight.
n.10: That is, a temple, where the basket would be set on a stand, as an idol is.
n.11: An old name for Babylonia (Genesis 11:2; Daniel 1:2), the place of exile and of the tower of Babel.

v: Again I looked up, and I saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains, and the mountains were mountains of bronze.[^1]
וָאָשֻׁ֗ב וָאֶשָּׂ֤א עֵינַי֙ וָֽאֶרְאֶ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה אַרְבַּ֤ע מַרְכָּבוֹת֙ יֹֽצְא֔וֹת מִבֵּ֖ין שְׁנֵ֣י הֶֽהָרִ֑ים וְהֶהָרִ֖ים הָרֵ֥י נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃
The first chariot had red horses, the second chariot black horses,
בַּמֶּרְכָּבָ֥ה הָרִֽאשֹׁנָ֖ה סוּסִ֣ים אֲדֻמִּ֑ים וּבַמֶּרְכָּבָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית סוּסִ֥ים שְׁחֹרִֽים׃
the third chariot white horses, and the fourth chariot dappled horses, all of them strong.[^2]
וּבַמֶּרְכָּבָ֥ה הַשְּׁלִשִׁ֖ית סוּסִ֣ים לְבָנִ֑ים וּבַמֶּרְכָּבָה֙ הָרְבִעִ֔ית סוּסִ֥ים בְּרֻדִּ֖ים אֲמֻצִּֽים׃
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these, my lord?"
וָאַ֙עַן֙ וָֽאֹמַ֔ר אֶל־הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ הַדֹּבֵ֣ר בִּ֑י מָה־אֵ֖לֶּה אֲדֹנִֽי׃
The angel answered me, "These are the four winds[^3] of heaven, going out after presenting themselves before the Lord of the whole earth.
וַיַּ֥עַן הַמַּלְאָ֖ךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֑י אֵ֗לֶּה אַרְבַּע֙ רֻח֣וֹת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם יוֹצְא֕וֹת מֵֽהִתְיַצֵּ֖ב עַל־אֲד֥וֹן כָּל־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
The chariot with the black horses is going out toward the land of the north, the white ones have gone out after them,[^4] and the dappled ones have gone out toward the land of the south."
אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֞הּ הַסּוּסִ֣ים הַשְּׁחֹרִ֗ים יֹֽצְאִים֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹן וְהַלְּבָנִ֔ים יָצְא֖וּ אֶל־אֽ͏ַחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם וְהַ֨בְּרֻדִּ֔ים יָצְא֖וּ אֶל־אֶ֥רֶץ הַתֵּימָֽן׃
When the strong ones[^5] went out, they were eager to go and patrol the earth. He said, "Go, patrol the earth!" So they patrolled the earth.
וְהָאֲמֻצִּ֣ים יָצְא֗וּ וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ לָלֶ֙כֶת֙ לְהִתְהַלֵּ֣ך בָּאָ֔רֶץ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לְכ֖וּ הִתְהַלְּכ֣וּ בָאָ֑רֶץ וַתִּתְהַלַּ֖כְנָה בָּאָֽרֶץ׃
Then he called to me and said to me, "Look, those going out toward the land of the north have given my Spirit rest[^6] in the land of the north."
וַיַּזְעֵ֣ק אֹתִ֔י וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר רְאֵ֗ה הַיּֽוֹצְאִים֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ צָפ֔וֹן הֵנִ֥יחוּ אֶת־רוּחִ֖י בְּאֶ֥רֶץ צָפֽוֹן׃ ס
The word of the LORD[^7] came to me:
וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
Take an offering from the exiles,[^8] from Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah, who have come from Babylon. Go that same day to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.
לָק֙וֹחַ֙ מֵאֵ֣ת הַגּוֹלָ֔ה מֵחֶלְדַּ֕י וּמֵאֵ֥ת טוֹבִיָּ֖ה וּמֵאֵ֣ת יְדַֽעְיָ֑ה וּבָאתָ֤ אַתָּה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וּבָ֗אתָ בֵּ֚ית יֹאשִׁיָּ֣ה בֶן־צְפַנְיָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖אוּ מִבָּבֶֽל׃
Take silver and gold and make crowns,[^9] and set the crown on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
וְלָקַחְתָּ֥ כֶֽסֶף־וְזָהָ֖ב וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ עֲטָר֑וֹת וְשַׂמְתָּ֗ בְּרֹ֛אשׁ יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בֶּן־יְהוֹצָדָ֖ק הַכֹּהֵ֥ן הַגָּדֽוֹל׃
Say to him: This is what the LORD of Armies[^10] says: Here is a man whose name is the Branch.[^11] He will branch out from his place, and he will build the temple of the LORD.
וְאָמַרְתָּ֤ אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּה־אִ֞ישׁ צֶ֤מַח שְׁמוֹ֙ וּמִתַּחְתָּ֣יו יִצְמָ֔ח וּבָנָ֖ה אֶת־הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָֽהּ׃

It is he who will build the temple of the LORD. He will be clothed with majesty, and he will sit and rule on his throne. There will be a priest on his throne,[^12] and there will be a counsel of peace between the two of them.
וְ֠הוּא יִבְנֶ֞ה אֶת־הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ וְהֽוּא־יִשָּׂ֣א ה֔וֹד וְיָשַׁ֥ב וּמָשַׁ֖ל עַל־כִּסְא֑וֹ וְהָיָ֤ה כֹהֵן֙ עַל־כִּסְא֔וֹ וַעֲצַ֣ת שָׁל֔וֹם תִּהְיֶ֖ה בֵּ֥ין שְׁנֵיהֶֽם׃
The crown will be a memorial in the temple of the LORD for Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah and Hen son of Zephaniah.[^13]
וְהָעֲטָרֹ֗ת תִּֽהְיֶה֙ לְחֵ֙לֶם֙ וּלְטוֹבִיָּ֣ה וְלִידַֽעְיָ֔ה וּלְחֵ֖ן בֶּן־צְפַנְיָ֑ה לְזִכָּר֖וֹן בְּהֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָֽה׃

Those who are far away will come and help to build the temple of the LORD. Then you will know that the LORD of Armies has sent me to you. This will happen if you carefully obey the voice of the LORD your God.[^14]
וּרְחוֹקִ֣ים ׀ יָבֹ֗אוּ וּבָנוּ֙ בְּהֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה וִידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּֽי־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁלָחַ֣נִי אֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וְהָיָה֙ אִם־שָׁמ֣וֹעַ תִּשְׁמְע֔וּן בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃ ס

n.1: Perhaps the gateway of heaven, from which the chariots go out. In the ancient Near East the sun was pictured as rising between two mountains.
n.2: Hebrew *amutsim*, "strong", perhaps a color: "piebald" or "gray". Compare the horses of 1:8.
n.4: Or "toward the west", with a small change to the Hebrew. The red horses are not mentioned.
n.5: Probably the dappled horses, or all four teams. Some scholars read "the red ones", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.6: That is, they have calmed my anger, or they have set my Spirit on the land of the north (compare Ezekiel 5:13). Hebrew *ruach* can mean spirit, wind or breath.
n.7: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.8: Literally "Take from the exile". These men had brought gifts from the Jews in Babylon.
n.9: Hebrew *atarot*, plural, perhaps one crown made of several circlets. Also in verse 14, where the verb is singular. Many scholars think the crown was meant for Zerubbabel, as the title "the Branch" suggests (3:8; Haggai 2:23), but no manuscript reads his name here.
n.10: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verse 15.
n.11: Hebrew *tsemach*, "sprout, growth", a title of a coming king of David's line (3:8). *He will branch out* is *yitsmach*, from the same word. The Aramaic Targum reads "the anointed one (Messiah)".
n.12: Or "He will be a priest on his throne". The Septuagint reads "and the priest will be at his right hand".
n.13: *Helem* is probably Heldai (verse 10), and *Hen*, "favor", perhaps another name for Josiah (verse 10), or "for the kindness of the son of Zephaniah".
n.14: The sentence is left unfinished in the Hebrew, as if to say, "This will happen, if …" Compare Deuteronomy 28:1.

v: In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the LORD[^1] came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Kislev.[^2]
וַֽיְהִי֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת אַרְבַּ֔ע לְדָרְיָ֖וֶשׁ הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ הָיָ֨ה דְבַר־יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־זְכַרְיָ֗ה בְּאַרְבָּעָ֛ה לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַתְּשִׁעִ֖י בְּכִסְלֵֽו׃
Now the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and their men[^3] to seek the favor of the LORD,[^4]
וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ בֵּֽית־אֵ֔ל שַׂר־אֶ֕צֶר וְרֶ֥גֶם מֶ֖לֶךְ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֑יו לְחַלּ֖וֹת אֶת־פְּנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃
and to ask the priests of the house of the LORD of Armies[^5] and the prophets, "Should I weep in the fifth month and abstain,[^6] as I have done for so many years?"
לֵאמֹ֗ר אֶל־הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֲשֶׁר֙ לְבֵית־יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְאֶל־הַנְּבִיאִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר הַֽאֶבְכֶּה֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַחֲמִשִׁ֔י הִנָּזֵ֕ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשִׂ֔יתִי זֶ֖ה כַּמֶּ֥ה שָׁנִֽים׃ פ
Then the word of the LORD of Armies came to me:
וַיְהִ֛י דְּבַר־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
Say to all the people of the land and to the priests: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth month and in the seventh month[^7] for these seventy years, was it really for me that you fasted?
אֱמֹר֙ אֶל־כָּל־עַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֶל־הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר כִּֽי־צַמְתֶּ֨ם וְסָפ֜וֹד בַּחֲמִישִׁ֣י וּבַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וְזֶה֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה הֲצ֥וֹם צַמְתֻּ֖נִי אָֽנִי׃
And when you eat and when you drink, are you not eating and drinking for yourselves?
וְכִ֥י תֹאכְל֖וּ וְכִ֣י תִשְׁתּ֑וּ הֲל֤וֹא אַתֶּם֙ הָאֹ֣כְלִ֔ים וְאַתֶּ֖ם הַשֹּׁתִֽים׃

Are not these the words that the LORD proclaimed through the earlier prophets,[^8] when Jerusalem was inhabited and at peace, with its towns around it, and when the Negev and the Shephelah[^9] were inhabited?
הֲל֣וֹא אֶת־הַדְּבָרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר קָרָ֤א יְהוָה֙ בְּיַד֙ הַנְּבִיאִ֣ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֔ים בִּהְי֤וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ יֹשֶׁ֣בֶת וּשְׁלֵוָ֔ה וְעָרֶ֖יהָ סְבִיבֹתֶ֑יהָ וְהַנֶּ֥גֶב וְהַשְּׁפֵלָ֖ה יֹשֵֽׁב׃ פ
The word of the LORD came to Zechariah:
וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־זְכַרְיָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃
This is what the LORD of Armies says: Judge with true justice; show faithful love[^10] and compassion to one another.[^11]
כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹ֑ר מִשְׁפַּ֤ט אֱמֶת֙ שְׁפֹ֔טוּ וְחֶ֣סֶד וְרַֽחֲמִ֔ים עֲשׂ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ אֶת־אָחִֽיו׃
Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the foreigner or the poor, and do not plot evil against one another in your hearts.
וְאַלְמָנָ֧ה וְיָת֛וֹם גֵּ֥ר וְעָנִ֖י אַֽל־תַּעֲשֹׁ֑קוּ וְרָעַת֙ אִ֣ישׁ אָחִ֔יו אַֽל־תַּחְשְׁב֖וּ בִּלְבַבְכֶֽם׃
But they refused to pay attention. They turned a stubborn shoulder[^12] and stopped their ears so as not to hear.
וַיְמָאֲנ֣וּ לְהַקְשִׁ֔יב וַיִּתְּנ֥וּ כָתֵ֖ף סֹרָ֑רֶת וְאָזְנֵיהֶ֖ם הִכְבִּ֥ידוּ מִשְּׁמֽוֹעַ׃

They made their hearts as hard as flint,[^13] so as not to hear the law[^14] and the words that the LORD of Armies had sent by his Spirit through the earlier prophets. So great anger came from the LORD of Armies.

וְלִבָּ֞ם שָׂ֣מוּ שָׁמִ֗יר מִ֠שְּׁמוֹעַ אֶת־הַתּוֹרָ֤ה וְאֶת־הַדְּבָרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁלַ֜ח יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ בְּרוּח֔וֹ בְּיַ֖ד הַנְּבִיאִ֣ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִ֑ים וַֽיְהִי֙ קֶ֣צֶף גָּד֔וֹל מֵאֵ֖ת יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
Just as I called[^15] and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen, says the LORD of Armies.
וַיְהִ֥י כַאֲשֶׁר־קָרָ֖א וְלֹ֣א שָׁמֵ֑עוּ כֵּ֤ן יִקְרְאוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א אֶשְׁמָ֔ע אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃
I scattered them with a storm among all the nations they had not known, and the land was left desolate behind them, with no one coming or going. So they made the pleasant land a desolation.
וְאֵ֣סָעֲרֵ֗ם עַ֤ל כָּל־הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־יְדָע֔וּם וְהָאָ֙רֶץ֙ נָשַׁ֣מָּה אַֽחֲרֵיהֶ֔ם מֵֽעֹבֵ֖ר וּמִשָּׁ֑ב וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ אֶֽרֶץ־חֶמְדָּ֖ה לְשַׁמָּֽה׃ פ

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: 7 December 518 BC. *Kislev* is the Babylonian name of the month.
n.3: Literally "Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and his men". Or "Bethel-sharezer sent Regem-melech and his men". Bethel, about 11 miles (18 km) north of Jerusalem, was resettled after the exile (Ezra 2:28).
n.4: Literally "to soften the face of the LORD", that is, to pray for his favor.
n.5: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.6: Literally "separate myself", that is, by fasting. The fast of the fifth month mourned the burning of the temple and of Jerusalem by the Babylonians (2 Kings 25:8–9; Jeremiah 52:12–13). Now that the temple was being rebuilt, the people asked whether to keep it.
n.7: The fast of the seventh month probably mourned the murder of Gedaliah, the governor appointed by Babylon (2 Kings 25:25; Jeremiah 41:1–3). Compare 8:19.
n.9: The dry south of Judah and the low hills to the west.
n.11: Literally "each to his brother". Also in verse 10.
n.12: Like an ox that will not take the yoke (Nehemiah 9:29; Hosea 4:16).
n.13: Hebrew *shamir*, a very hard stone, perhaps emery or diamond (Jeremiah 17:1; Ezekiel 3:9).
n.15: Literally "Just as he called". The Hebrew moves from the LORD speaking of himself as "he" to "I".

v: The word of the LORD of Armies[^1] came:
וַיְהִ֛י דְּבַר־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת לֵאמֹֽר׃
This is what the LORD of Armies says: I am very jealous for Zion; I am jealous for her with great fury.[^2]
כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת קִנֵּ֥אתִי לְצִיּ֖וֹן קִנְאָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וְחֵמָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה קִנֵּ֥אתִי לָֽהּ׃

This is what the LORD says: I have returned to Zion, and I will live in the middle of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the City of Faithfulness,[^3] and the mountain of the LORD of Armies the Holy Mountain.
כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה שַׁ֚בְתִּי אֶל־צִיּ֔וֹן וְשָׁכַנְתִּ֖י בְּת֣וֹךְ יְרֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְנִקְרְאָ֤ה יְרוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ עִ֣יר־הָֽאֱמֶ֔ת וְהַר־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת הַ֥ר הַקֹּֽדֶשׁ׃ ס
This is what the LORD of Armies says: Old men and old women will again sit in the squares of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of great age.
כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת עֹ֤ד יֵֽשְׁבוּ֙ זְקֵנִ֣ים וּזְקֵנ֔וֹת בִּרְחֹב֖וֹת יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְאִ֧ישׁ מִשְׁעַנְתּ֛וֹ בְּיָד֖וֹ מֵרֹ֥ב יָמִֽים׃
And the squares of the city will be full of boys and girls playing there.
וּרְחֹב֤וֹת הָעִיר֙ יִמָּ֣לְא֔וּ יְלָדִ֖ים וִֽילָד֑וֹת מְשַׂחֲקִ֖ים בִּרְחֹֽבֹתֶֽיהָ׃ ס

This is what the LORD of Armies says: If it seems too wonderful[^4] in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, must it also seem too wonderful in my eyes? declares the LORD of Armies.[^5]
כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת כִּ֣י יִפָּלֵ֗א בְּעֵינֵי֙ שְׁאֵרִית֙ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה בַּיָּמִ֖ים הָהֵ֑ם גַּם־בְּעֵינַי֙ יִפָּלֵ֔א נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ פ
This is what the LORD of Armies says: I am going to save my people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting sun.
כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת הִנְנִ֥י מוֹשִׁ֛יעַ אֶת־עַמִּ֖י מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִזְרָ֑ח וּמֵאֶ֖רֶץ מְב֥וֹא הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
I will bring them to live in the middle of Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God,[^6] in faithfulness and righteousness.
וְהֵבֵאתִ֣י אֹתָ֔ם וְשָׁכְנ֖וּ בְּת֣וֹךְ יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְהָיוּ־לִ֣י לְעָ֗ם וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֶהְיֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לֵֽאלֹהִ֔ים בֶּאֱמֶ֖ת וּבִצְדָקָֽה׃ ס

This is what the LORD of Armies says: Let your hands be strong, you who in these days are hearing these words from the mouth of the prophets[^7] who spoke on the day the foundation was laid for the house of the LORD of Armies, so that the temple might be built.

כֹּֽה־אָמַר֮ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֒ תֶּחֱזַ֣קְנָה יְדֵיכֶ֔ם הַשֹּֽׁמְעִים֙ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֵ֖ת הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה מִפִּי֙ הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים אֲ֠שֶׁר בְּי֞וֹם יֻסַּ֨ד בֵּית־יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת הַהֵיכָ֖ל לְהִבָּנֽוֹת׃
For before those days there were no wages for people or for animals, and no one who went out or came in was safe from the enemy,[^8] for I set everyone against his neighbor.
כִּ֗י לִפְנֵי֙ הַיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם שְׂכַ֤ר הָֽאָדָם֙ לֹ֣א נִֽהְיָ֔ה וּשְׂכַ֥ר הַבְּהֵמָ֖ה אֵינֶ֑נָּה וְלַיּוֹצֵ֨א וְלַבָּ֤א אֵין־שָׁלוֹם֙ מִן־הַצָּ֔ר וַאֲשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת־כָּל־הָאָדָ֖ם אִ֥ישׁ בְּרֵעֵֽהוּ׃
But now I will not treat the remnant of this people as in the former days, declares the LORD of Armies.
וְעַתָּ֗ה לֹ֣א כַיָּמִ֤ים הָרִֽאשֹׁנִים֙ אֲנִ֔י לִשְׁאֵרִ֖ית הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

For there will be a sowing in peace:[^9] the vine will give its fruit, the earth will give its produce, and the heavens will give their dew. I will give the remnant of this people all these things to possess.
כִּֽי־זֶ֣רַע הַשָּׁל֗וֹם הַגֶּ֜פֶן תִּתֵּ֤ן פִּרְיָהּ֙ וְהָאָ֙רֶץ֙ תִּתֵּ֣ן אֶת־יְבוּלָ֔הּ וְהַשָּׁמַ֖יִם יִתְּנ֣וּ טַלָּ֑ם וְהִנְחַלְתִּ֗י אֶת־שְׁאֵרִ֛ית הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּ֖ה אֶת־כָּל־אֵֽלֶּה׃
As you have been a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be a blessing.[^10] Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.
וְהָיָ֡ה כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ הֱיִיתֶ֨ם קְלָלָ֜ה בַּגּוֹיִ֗ם בֵּ֤ית יְהוּדָה֙ וּבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֵּ֚ן אוֹשִׁ֣יעַ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וִהְיִיתֶ֖ם בְּרָכָ֑ה אַל־תִּירָ֖אוּ תֶּחֱזַ֥קְנָה יְדֵיכֶֽם׃ ס
For this is what the LORD of Armies says: Just as I planned to bring disaster on you when your ancestors made me angry, says the LORD of Armies, and I did not relent,
כִּ֣י כֹ֣ה אָמַר֮ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֒ כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר זָמַמְ֜תִּי לְהָרַ֣ע לָכֶ֗ם בְּהַקְצִ֤יף אֲבֹֽתֵיכֶם֙ אֹתִ֔י אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְלֹ֖א נִחָֽמְתִּי׃
so now in these days I have again planned to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.
כֵּ֣ן שַׁ֤בְתִּי זָמַ֙מְתִּי֙ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה לְהֵיטִ֥יב אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם וְאֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה אַל־תִּירָֽאוּ׃
These are the things you are to do: Speak the truth to one another;[^11] in your gates give judgments that are true and make for peace.
אֵ֥לֶּה הַדְּבָרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּֽעֲשׂ֑וּ דַּבְּר֤וּ אֱמֶת֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־רֵעֵ֔הוּ אֱמֶת֙ וּמִשְׁפַּ֣ט שָׁל֔וֹם שִׁפְט֖וּ בְּשַׁעֲרֵיכֶֽם׃
Do not plot evil against one another in your hearts, and do not love a false oath, for all these are things that I hate, declares the LORD.
וְאִ֣ישׁ ׀ אֶת־רָעַ֣ת רֵעֵ֗הוּ אַֽל־תַּחְשְׁבוּ֙ בִּלְבַבְכֶ֔ם וּשְׁבֻ֥עַת שֶׁ֖קֶר אַֽל־תֶּאֱהָ֑בוּ כִּ֧י אֶת־כָּל־אֵ֛לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׂנֵ֖אתִי נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃ ס
The word of the LORD of Armies came to me:
וַיְהִ֛י דְּבַר־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃

This is what the LORD of Armies says: The fasts of the fourth month, the fifth, the seventh and the tenth[^12] will become times of joy and gladness and cheerful festivals for the house of Judah. So love truth and peace.

כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת צ֣וֹם הָרְבִיעִ֡י וְצ֣וֹם הַחֲמִישִׁי֩ וְצ֨וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֜י וְצ֣וֹם הָעֲשִׂירִ֗י יִהְיֶ֤ה לְבֵית־יְהוּדָה֙ לְשָׂשׂ֣וֹן וּלְשִׂמְחָ֔ה וּֽלְמֹעֲדִ֖ים טוֹבִ֑ים וְהָאֱמֶ֥ת וְהַשָּׁל֖וֹם אֱהָֽבוּ׃ פ
This is what the LORD of Armies says: Peoples will yet come, the inhabitants of many cities.
כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת עֹ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר יָבֹ֣אוּ עַמִּ֔ים וְיֹשְׁבֵ֖י עָרִ֥ים רַבּֽוֹת׃
The inhabitants of one city will go to another and say, "Let us go at once to seek the favor of the LORD[^13] and to seek the LORD of Armies. I am going too."
וְֽהָלְכ֡וּ יֹשְׁבֵי֩ אַחַ֨ת אֶל־אַחַ֜ת לֵאמֹ֗ר נֵלְכָ֤ה הָלוֹךְ֙ לְחַלּוֹת֙ אֶת־פְּנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וּלְבַקֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אֵלְכָ֖ה גַּם־אָֽנִי׃
Many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the LORD of Armies in Jerusalem and to seek the favor of the LORD.
וּבָ֨אוּ עַמִּ֤ים רַבִּים֙ וְגוֹיִ֣ם עֲצוּמִ֔ים לְבַקֵּ֛שׁ אֶת־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בִּירוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וּלְחַלּ֖וֹת אֶת־פְּנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃ ס

This is what the LORD of Armies says: In those days ten men from nations of every language will take hold, they will take hold of the hem[^14] of a Jew and say, "Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you."

כֹּ֥ה אָמַר֮ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֒ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔מָּה אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַחֲזִ֙יקוּ֙ עֲשָׂרָ֣ה אֲנָשִׁ֔ים מִכֹּ֖ל לְשֹׁנ֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְֽהֶחֱזִ֡יקוּ בִּכְנַף֩ אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדִ֜י לֵאמֹ֗ר נֵֽלְכָה֙ עִמָּכֶ֔ם כִּ֥י שָׁמַ֖עְנוּ אֱלֹהִ֥ים עִמָּכֶֽם׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. The chapter is made up of ten sayings, each beginning "This is what the LORD (of Armies) says".
n.3: Or "the City of Truth". Hebrew *emet*, "faithfulness, truth". Compare Isaiah 1:26.
n.4: Or "too hard". The same Hebrew verb is used in Genesis 18:14: "Is anything too hard for the LORD?"
n.5: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH tseva'ot*, "the declaration of the LORD of Armies", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. Also in verses 11 and 17.
n.6: The words of the covenant (Jeremiah 31:33; Ezekiel 36:28).
n.9: Literally "the seed of peace". The Hebrew is difficult.
n.10: Compare Genesis 12:2–3, and the curse of Jeremiah 24:9.
n.11: Literally "each with his neighbor". Ephesians 4:25 quotes these words.
n.12: These fasts mourned the fall of Jerusalem: the breach in its wall in the fourth month (2 Kings 25:3–4; Jeremiah 39:2), the burning of the temple in the fifth (7:3), the murder of Gedaliah in the seventh (7:5), and the start of the siege in the tenth (2 Kings 25:1).
n.13: Literally "to soften the face of the LORD", as in 7:2. Also in verse 22.
n.14: Hebrew *kanaf*, the corner of the robe, where the tassels that reminded Israelites of the LORD's commands were worn (Numbers 15:38–39).

v: An oracle.[^1] The word of the LORD[^2] is against the land of Hadrach,[^3] and Damascus is where it comes to rest. For the eyes of humankind and of all the tribes of Israel are on the LORD.[^4]
מַשָּׂ֤א דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חַדְרָ֔ךְ וְדַמֶּ֖שֶׂק מְנֻחָת֑וֹ כִּ֤י לַֽיהוָה֙ עֵ֣ין אָדָ֔ם וְכֹ֖ל שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
It is against Hamath too, which borders on it, and against Tyre and Sidon, though they are very wise.
וְגַם־חֲמָ֖ת תִּגְבָּל־בָּ֑הּ צֹ֣ר וְצִיד֔וֹן כִּ֥י חָֽכְמָ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃
Tyre has built herself a fortress[^5] and heaped up silver like dust and gold like the mud of the streets.
וַתִּ֥בֶן צֹ֛ר מָצ֖וֹר לָ֑הּ וַתִּצְבָּר־כֶּ֙סֶף֙ כֶּֽעָפָ֔ר וְחָר֖וּץ כְּטִ֥יט חוּצֽוֹת׃
But look, the Lord[^6] will take possession of her and strike down her power on the sea,[^7] and she will be devoured by fire.
הִנֵּ֤ה אֲדֹנָי֙ יֽוֹרִשֶׁ֔נָּה וְהִכָּ֥ה בַיָּ֖ם חֵילָ֑הּ וְהִ֖יא בָּאֵ֥שׁ תֵּאָכֵֽל׃
Ashkelon will see it and be afraid; Gaza too will writhe in anguish, and Ekron, for her hope will be put to shame. Gaza will lose her king, and Ashkelon will be uninhabited.
תֵּרֶ֨א אַשְׁקְל֜וֹן וְתִירָ֗א וְעַזָּה֙ וְתָחִ֣יל מְאֹ֔ד וְעֶקְר֖וֹן כִּֽי־הֹבִ֣ישׁ מֶבָּטָ֑הּ וְאָ֤בַד מֶ֙לֶךְ֙ מֵֽעַזָּ֔ה וְאַשְׁקְל֖וֹן לֹ֥א תֵשֵֽׁב׃
A people of mixed race[^8] will live in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
וְיָשַׁ֥ב מַמְזֵ֖ר בְּאַשְׁדּ֑וֹד וְהִכְרַתִּ֖י גְּא֥וֹן פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים׃

I will take the blood out of his mouth and the detestable food from between his teeth.[^9] He too will be a remnant for our God. He will be like a clan[^10] in Judah, and Ekron like the Jebusites.[^11]
וַהֲסִרֹתִ֨י דָמָ֜יו מִפִּ֗יו וְשִׁקֻּצָיו֙ מִבֵּ֣ין שִׁנָּ֔יו וְנִשְׁאַ֥ר גַּם־ה֖וּא לֵֽאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְהָיָה֙ כְּאַלֻּ֣ף בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְעֶקְר֖וֹן כִּיבוּסִֽי׃
I will camp around my house as a guard,[^12] against those who march back and forth. No oppressor will overrun them again, for now I have seen with my own eyes.
וְחָנִ֨יתִי לְבֵיתִ֤י מִצָּבָה֙ מֵעֹבֵ֣ר וּמִשָּׁ֔ב וְלֹֽא־יַעֲבֹ֧ר עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם ע֖וֹד נֹגֵ֑שׂ כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה רָאִ֥יתִי בְעֵינָֽי׃ ס

Rejoice greatly, Daughter Zion![^13] Shout, Daughter Jerusalem! Look, your king is coming to you, righteous and victorious,[^14] humble[^15] and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.[^16]
גִּילִ֨י מְאֹ֜ד בַּת־צִיּ֗וֹן הָרִ֙יעִי֙ בַּ֣ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם הִנֵּ֤ה מַלְכֵּךְ֙ יָ֣בוֹא לָ֔ךְ צַדִּ֥יק וְנוֹשָׁ֖ע ה֑וּא עָנִי֙ וְרֹכֵ֣ב עַל־חֲמ֔וֹר וְעַל־עַ֖יִר בֶּן־אֲתֹנֽוֹת׃

I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the war horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow will be cut off. He will proclaim peace to the nations. His rule will be from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.[^17]
וְהִכְרַתִּי־רֶ֣כֶב מֵאֶפְרַ֗יִם וְסוּס֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְנִכְרְתָה֙ קֶ֣שֶׁת מִלְחָמָ֔ה וְדִבֶּ֥ר שָׁל֖וֹם לַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּמָשְׁלוֹ֙ מִיָּ֣ם עַד־יָ֔ם וּמִנָּהָ֖ר עַד־אַפְסֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃
As for you, because of the blood of my covenant with you,[^18] I will set your prisoners free from the waterless pit.[^19]
גַּם־אַ֣תְּ בְּדַם־בְּרִיתֵ֗ךְ שִׁלַּ֤חְתִּי אֲסִירַ֙יִךְ֙ מִבּ֔וֹר אֵ֥ין מַ֖יִם בּֽוֹ׃
Return to the stronghold, you prisoners of hope. Even today I declare that I will give back to you double.[^20]
שׁ֚וּבוּ לְבִצָּר֔וֹן אֲסִירֵ֖י הַתִּקְוָ֑ה גַּם־הַיּ֕וֹם מַגִּ֥יד מִשְׁנֶ֖ה אָשִׁ֥יב לָֽךְ׃
For I will bend Judah as my bow; I will fill it with Ephraim as its arrow.[^21] I will rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece,[^22] and make you like a warrior's sword.
כִּֽי־דָרַ֨כְתִּי לִ֜י יְהוּדָ֗ה קֶ֚שֶׁת מִלֵּ֣אתִי אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְעוֹרַרְתִּ֤י בָנַ֙יִךְ֙ צִיּ֔וֹן עַל־בָּנַ֖יִךְ יָוָ֑ן וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךְ כְּחֶ֥רֶב גִּבּֽוֹר׃
Then the LORD will appear over them, and his arrow will flash like lightning. The Lord GOD[^23] will blow the ram's horn[^24] and march out in the storms of the south.[^25]
וַֽיהוָה֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם יֵֽרָאֶ֔ה וְיָצָ֥א כַבָּרָ֖ק חִצּ֑וֹ וַֽאדֹנָ֤י יְהֹוִה֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֣ר יִתְקָ֔ע וְהָלַ֖ךְ בְּסַעֲר֥וֹת תֵּימָֽן׃

The LORD of Armies[^26] will shield them. They will devour and trample the sling stones;[^27] they will drink and roar as if with wine. They will be full like a bowl, like the corners of the altar.[^28]
יְהוָ֣ה צְבָאוֹת֮ יָגֵ֣ן עֲלֵיהֶם֒ וְאָכְל֗וּ וְכָֽבְשׁוּ֙ אַבְנֵי־קֶ֔לַע וְשָׁת֥וּ הָמ֖וּ כְּמוֹ־יָ֑יִן וּמָֽלְאוּ֙ כַּמִּזְרָ֔ק כְּזָוִיּ֖וֹת מִזְבֵּֽחַ׃
On that day the LORD their God will save them, as the flock of his people. For like the jewels of a crown they will sparkle over his land.
וְֽהוֹשִׁיעָ֞ם יְהוָ֧ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כְּצֹ֣אן עַמּ֑וֹ כִּ֚י אַבְנֵי־נֵ֔זֶר מִֽתְנוֹסְס֖וֹת עַל־אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃
How good and how beautiful it will be![^29] Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine the young women.
כִּ֥י מַה־טּוּב֖וֹ וּמַה־יָפְי֑וֹ דָּגָן֙ בַּֽחוּרִ֔ים וְתִיר֖וֹשׁ יְנוֹבֵ֥ב בְּתֻלֽוֹת׃

n.1: Hebrew *massa*, from the verb "to lift up, carry": a message "lifted up" by the prophet, or a "burden" laid on a nation. Traditionally "the burden". The same heading begins chapters 12–14 and the book of Malachi. Chapters 9–14 have no dates and no visions, and many scholars think they come from a later time than chapters 1–8.
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: A city-state in northern Syria, known from Assyrian records as Hatarikka.
n.4: Or "For the LORD has an eye on humankind, as on all the tribes of Israel". Literally "For to the LORD is the eye of humankind". Some scholars read "the eye of Aram", with a small change to the Hebrew.
n.5: A play on words: *Tsor*, "Tyre", and *matsor*, "fortress". Tyre stood on an island off the coast.
n.6: Hebrew *Adonai*, "the Lord", not the name YHWH.
n.7: Or "strike her wealth into the sea" or "her rampart into the sea".
n.8: Hebrew *mamzer*, a person of forbidden or mixed birth (Deuteronomy 23:3, 23:2 in most English Bibles).
n.9: Meat eaten with its blood, and other food that was unclean to Israel (Leviticus 11; 17:10–14). The Philistines will be cleansed and become part of the LORD's people.
n.10: Hebrew *alluf*, a clan or a clan chief.
n.11: The people of Jerusalem before David took it, who lived on among the people of Judah (2 Samuel 5:6–9; 24:18–24).
n.12: Hebrew *mitsavah*, perhaps "against an army". The meaning is uncertain.
n.13: A poetic name for Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a young woman. So also *Daughter Jerusalem*.
n.14: Literally "saved", that is, given victory by the LORD. The Septuagint reads "saving".
n.15: Hebrew *ani*, "poor, afflicted, humble". The Septuagint reads "gentle".
n.16: Literally "on a male donkey, on a colt, the son of she-donkeys". The two phrases describe one animal, as Hebrew poetry often says one thing twice. Matthew 21:5 and John 12:15 quote this verse of Jesus' entry into Jerusalem, which Mark 11:1–10 also tells, and Matthew speaks of a donkey and a colt.
n.17: The same words are found in Psalm 72:8. *The River* is the Euphrates.
n.18: Literally "the blood of your covenant", the covenant sealed with the blood of sacrifice (Exodus 24:8). The Hebrew is feminine, addressing Zion.
n.19: Hebrew *bor*, a pit or empty cistern, used as a prison (Genesis 37:24; Jeremiah 38:6).
n.21: Literally "I will fill the bow with Ephraim".
n.22: Hebrew *Yavan*, Ionia, the Greeks of the Aegean coasts (Ezekiel 27:13; Joel 4:6, 3:6 in most English Bibles).
n.23: Hebrew *Adonai YHWH*, "my Lord YHWH". After "Lord", God's personal name is written GOD in capitals, as in most English Bibles.
n.24: Hebrew *shofar*, a trumpet made from a ram's horn, sounded as an alarm in war.
n.25: Hebrew *teman*, the south, also the region of Teman in Edom, from which the LORD comes in Habakkuk 3:3.
n.26: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.27: The Hebrew of this verse is difficult. Or "They will devour, and the sling stones will conquer".
n.28: The bowls held the blood of the sacrifices, which was splashed on the corners of the altar (Exodus 27:3; Leviticus 4:7).
n.29: Literally "How great is his goodness, and how great his beauty!" *His* may be the LORD or the people.

v: Ask the LORD[^1] for rain in the season of the spring rain.[^2] It is the LORD who makes the storm clouds, and he will give them showers of rain, and plants in the field for everyone.
שַׁאֲל֨וּ מֵיְהוָ֤ה מָטָר֙ בְּעֵ֣ת מַלְק֔וֹשׁ יְהוָ֖ה עֹשֶׂ֣ה חֲזִיזִ֑ים וּמְטַר־גֶּ֙שֶׁם֙ יִתֵּ֣ן לָהֶ֔ם לְאִ֖ישׁ עֵ֥שֶׂב בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃
For the household gods[^3] speak nonsense, and the diviners see lies. They tell false dreams and give empty comfort. So the people wander like sheep; they suffer for lack of a shepherd.[^4]
כִּ֧י הַתְּרָפִ֣ים דִּבְּרוּ־אָ֗וֶן וְהַקּֽוֹסְמִים֙ חָ֣זוּ שֶׁ֔קֶר וַֽחֲלֹמוֹת֙ הַשָּׁ֣וא יְדַבֵּ֔רוּ הֶ֖בֶל יְנַֽחֵמ֑וּן עַל־כֵּן֙ נָסְע֣וּ כְמוֹ־צֹ֔אן יַעֲנ֖וּ כִּֽי־אֵ֥ין רֹעֶֽה׃ פ

My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will punish the leaders.[^5] For the LORD of Armies[^6] cares for his flock,[^7] the house of Judah, and he will make them like his majestic horse in battle.
עַל־הָֽרֹעִים֙ חָרָ֣ה אַפִּ֔י וְעַל־הָעַתּוּדִ֖ים אֶפְק֑וֹד כִּֽי־פָקַד֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֤וֹת אֶת־עֶדְרוֹ֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה וְשָׂ֣ם אוֹתָ֔ם כְּס֥וּס הוֹד֖וֹ בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה׃
From Judah[^8] will come the cornerstone, from Judah the tent peg, from Judah the battle bow, from Judah every ruler,[^9] all together.
מִמֶּ֤נּוּ פִנָּה֙ מִמֶּ֣נּוּ יָתֵ֔ד מִמֶּ֖נּוּ קֶ֣שֶׁת מִלְחָמָ֑ה מִמֶּ֛נּוּ יֵצֵ֥א כָל־נוֹגֵ֖שׂ יַחְדָּֽו׃
They will be like warriors trampling the enemy into the mud of the streets in battle. They will fight, because the LORD is with them, and they will put the horsemen to shame.
וְהָי֨וּ כְגִבֹּרִ֜ים בּוֹסִ֨ים בְּטִ֤יט חוּצוֹת֙ בַּמִּלְחָמָ֔ה וְנִ֨לְחֲמ֔וּ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה עִמָּ֑ם וְהֹבִ֖ישׁוּ רֹכְבֵ֥י סוּסִֽים׃

I will strengthen the house of Judah and save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back[^10] because I have compassion on them, and they will be as though I had never rejected them. For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
וְגִבַּרְתִּ֣י ׀ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֗ה וְאֶת־בֵּ֤ית יוֹסֵף֙ אוֹשִׁ֔יעַ וְהֽוֹשְׁבוֹתִים֙ כִּ֣י רִֽחַמְתִּ֔ים וְהָי֖וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־זְנַחְתִּ֑ים כִּ֗י אֲנִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיהֶ֖ם וְאֶעֱנֵֽם׃
Ephraim will be like a warrior, and their hearts will be glad as with wine. Their children will see it and be glad; their hearts will rejoice in the LORD.
וְהָי֤וּ כְגִבּוֹר֙ אֶפְרַ֔יִם וְשָׂמַ֥ח לִבָּ֖ם כְּמוֹ־יָ֑יִן וּבְנֵיהֶם֙ יִרְא֣וּ וְשָׂמֵ֔חוּ יָגֵ֥ל לִבָּ֖ם בַּיהוָֽה׃
I will whistle for them[^11] and gather them in, for I have redeemed them, and they will be as many as they were before.
אֶשְׁרְקָ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם וַאֲקַבְּצֵ֖ם כִּ֣י פְדִיתִ֑ים וְרָב֖וּ כְּמ֥וֹ רָבֽוּ׃
Though I scattered them like seed[^12] among the peoples, in far countries they will remember me. They and their children will live, and they will return.
וְאֶזְרָעֵם֙ בָּֽעַמִּ֔ים וּבַמֶּרְחַקִּ֖ים יִזְכְּר֑וּנִי וְחָי֥וּ אֶת־בְּנֵיהֶ֖ם וָשָֽׁבוּ׃
I will bring them back from the land of Egypt and gather them from Assyria. I will bring them to the land of Gilead and to Lebanon,[^13] until there is no room left for them.
וַהֲשִֽׁיבוֹתִים֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּמֵֽאַשּׁ֖וּר אֲקַבְּצֵ֑ם וְאֶל־אֶ֨רֶץ גִּלְעָ֤ד וּלְבָנוֹן֙ אֲבִיאֵ֔ם וְלֹ֥א יִמָּצֵ֖א לָהֶֽם׃

He will pass through the sea of distress[^14] and strike the waves of the sea, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up. The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart.[^15]
וְעָבַ֨ר בַּיָּ֜ם צָרָ֗ה וְהִכָּ֤ה בַיָּם֙ גַּלִּ֔ים וְהֹבִ֕ישׁוּ כֹּ֖ל מְצוּל֣וֹת יְאֹ֑ר וְהוּרַד֙ גְּא֣וֹן אַשּׁ֔וּר וְשֵׁ֥בֶט מִצְרַ֖יִם יָסֽוּר׃
I will strengthen them in the LORD, and they will walk in his name, declares the LORD.[^16]
וְגִבַּרְתִּים֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וּבִשְׁמ֖וֹ יִתְהַלָּ֑כוּ נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָֽה׃ ס

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Hebrew *malqosh*, the spring rain of March and April, which ripens the crops before the harvest.
n.3: Hebrew *teraphim*, images kept in the home and consulted for guidance (Genesis 31:19; Ezekiel 21:26, 21:21 in most English Bibles).
n.5: Literally "the male goats", the leaders of the flock (Isaiah 14:9; Jeremiah 50:8). The verb *paqad* means "punish" here and "care for" in the next line.
n.6: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.7: The same Hebrew verb, *paqad*, as *punish* in the first line.
n.8: Literally "from him", that is, from Judah. The cornerstone and the tent peg are pictures of leaders on whom the people rely (Isaiah 22:23; Psalm 118:22).
n.9: Hebrew *noges*, a word usually used of an oppressor or taskmaster (9:8).
n.10: The Hebrew word, *ve-hoshevotim*, seems to combine "I will bring them back" and "I will settle them".
n.11: Like a shepherd calling his flock (compare Isaiah 5:26; 7:18).
n.12: Literally "I will sow them". Compare Hosea 2:25 (2:23 in most English Bibles).
n.13: Gilead, east of the Jordan, and Lebanon, in the north, had been part of the land of the northern tribes.
n.14: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "He will pass through the sea, distress". The words recall the crossing of the Red Sea at the exodus.
n.16: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement.

v: Open your doors, Lebanon, so that fire may devour your cedars!
פְּתַ֥ח לְבָנ֖וֹן דְּלָתֶ֑יךָ וְתֹאכַ֥ל אֵ֖שׁ בַּאֲרָזֶֽיךָ׃
Wail, you cypress, for the cedar has fallen, for the mighty trees are ruined! Wail, you oaks of Bashan, for the dense forest[^1] has come down!
הֵילֵ֤ל בְּרוֹשׁ֙ כִּֽי־נָ֣פַל אֶ֔רֶז אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַדִּרִ֖ים שֻׁדָּ֑דוּ הֵילִ֙ילוּ֙ אַלּוֹנֵ֣י בָשָׁ֔ן כִּ֥י יָרַ֖ד יַ֥עַר *הבצור **הַבָּצִֽיר׃
Listen! The wailing of the shepherds, for their glory[^2] is ruined! Listen! The roaring of young lions, for the thickets of the Jordan[^3] are ruined!
ק֚וֹל יִֽלְלַ֣ת הָרֹעִ֔ים כִּ֥י שֻׁדְּדָ֖ה אַדַּרְתָּ֑ם ק֚וֹל שַׁאֲגַ֣ת כְּפִירִ֔ים כִּ֥י שֻׁדַּ֖ד גְּא֥וֹן הַיַּרְדֵּֽן׃ ס
This is what the LORD[^4] my God said: "Shepherd the flock marked for slaughter.[^5]
כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑י רְעֵ֖ה אֶת־צֹ֥אן הַהֲרֵגָֽה׃
Those who buy them kill them and go unpunished. Those who sell them say, 'Blessed be the LORD, for I am rich!' And their own shepherds have no pity on them.
אֲשֶׁ֨ר קֹנֵיהֶ֤ן יַֽהֲרְגֻן֙ וְלֹ֣א יֶאְשָׁ֔מוּ וּמֹכְרֵיהֶ֣ן יֹאמַ֔ר בָּר֥וּךְ יְהוָ֖ה וַאעְשִׁ֑ר וְרֹ֣עֵיהֶ֔ם לֹ֥א יַחְמ֖וֹל עֲלֵיהֶֽן׃

For I will no longer have pity on the people of the land, declares the LORD.[^6] Look, I am going to hand over everyone to his neighbor[^7] and to his king. They will crush the land, and I will not rescue anyone from their hand."

כִּ֠י לֹ֣א אֶחְמ֥וֹל ע֛וֹד עַל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י הָאָ֖רֶץ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְהִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י מַמְצִ֣יא אֶת־הָאָדָ֗ם אִ֤ישׁ בְּיַד־רֵעֵ֙הוּ֙ וּבְיַ֣ד מַלְכּ֔וֹ וְכִתְּתוּ֙ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹ֥א אַצִּ֖יל מִיָּדָֽם׃
So I shepherded the flock marked for slaughter, the most afflicted of the flock.[^8] I took two staffs. One I called Favor and the other I called Union,[^9] and I shepherded the flock.
וָֽאֶרְעֶה֙ אֶת־צֹ֣אן הַֽהֲרֵגָ֔ה לָכֵ֖ן עֲנִיֵּ֣י הַצֹּ֑אן וָאֶקַּֽח־לִ֞י שְׁנֵ֣י מַקְל֗וֹת לְאַחַ֞ד קָרָ֤אתִי נֹ֙עַם֙ וּלְאַחַד֙ קָרָ֣אתִי חֹֽבְלִ֔ים וָאֶרְעֶ֖ה אֶת־הַצֹּֽאן׃
In one month I got rid of the three shepherds.[^10] I lost patience with them,[^11] and they also detested me.
וָאַכְחִ֛ד אֶת־שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הָרֹעִ֖ים בְּיֶ֣רַח אֶחָ֑ד וַתִּקְצַ֤ר נַפְשִׁי֙ בָּהֶ֔ם וְגַם־נַפְשָׁ֖ם בָּחֲלָ֥ה בִֽי׃
Then I said, "I will not be your shepherd. Let the dying die, and let the perishing perish, and let those who are left devour one another's flesh."
וָאֹמַ֕ר לֹ֥א אֶרְעֶ֖ה אֶתְכֶ֑ם הַמֵּתָ֣ה תָמ֗וּת וְהַנִּכְחֶ֙דֶת֙ תִּכָּחֵ֔ד וְהַ֨נִּשְׁאָר֔וֹת תֹּאכַ֕לְנָה אִשָּׁ֖ה אֶת־בְּשַׂ֥ר רְעוּתָֽהּ׃
Then I took my staff Favor and broke it, to revoke the covenant I had made with all the peoples.
וָאֶקַּ֤ח אֶת־מַקְלִי֙ אֶת־נֹ֔עַם וָאֶגְדַּ֖ע אֹת֑וֹ לְהָפֵיר֙ אֶת־בְּרִיתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר כָּרַ֖תִּי אֶת־כָּל־הָעַמִּֽים׃
So it was revoked on that day, and the afflicted of the flock,[^12] who were watching me, knew that it was the word of the LORD.
וַתֻּפַ֖ר בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיֵּדְע֨וּ כֵ֜ן עֲנִיֵּ֤י הַצֹּאן֙ הַשֹּׁמְרִ֣ים אֹתִ֔י כִּ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃
Then I said to them, "If it seems good to you, give me my wages; if not, keep them." So they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver.[^13]
וָאֹמַ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם אִם־ט֧וֹב בְּעֵינֵיכֶ֛ם הָב֥וּ שְׂכָרִ֖י וְאִם־לֹ֣א ׀ חֲדָ֑לוּ וַיִּשְׁקְל֥וּ אֶת־שְׂכָרִ֖י שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים כָּֽסֶף׃

Then the LORD said to me, "Throw it to the potter,[^14] that magnificent price at which they valued me!"[^15] So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the house of the LORD, to the potter.
וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י הַשְׁלִיכֵ֙הוּ֙ אֶל־הַיּוֹצֵ֔ר אֶ֣דֶר הַיְקָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָקַ֖רְתִּי מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וָֽאֶקְחָה֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים הַכֶּ֔סֶף וָאַשְׁלִ֥יךְ אֹת֛וֹ בֵּ֥ית יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־הַיּוֹצֵֽר׃
Then I broke my second staff, Union, to revoke the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
וָֽאֶגְדַּע֙ אֶת־מַקְלִ֣י הַשֵּׁנִ֔י אֵ֖ת הַחֹֽבְלִ֑ים לְהָפֵר֙ אֶת־הָֽאַחֲוָ֔ה בֵּ֥ין יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבֵ֥ין יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ ס
Then the LORD said to me, "Take once more the equipment of a foolish shepherd.[^16]
וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י ע֣וֹד קַח־לְךָ֔ כְּלִ֖י רֹעֶ֥ה אֱוִלִֽי׃

For look, I am going to raise up a shepherd in the land who will not care for those that are perishing or seek the young[^17] or heal the injured or feed the healthy, but will eat the flesh of the fat ones and tear off their hooves.[^18]

כִּ֣י הִנֵּֽה־אָנֹכִי֩ מֵקִ֨ים רֹעֶ֜ה בָּאָ֗רֶץ הַנִּכְחָד֤וֹת לֹֽא־יִפְקֹד֙ הַנַּ֣עַר לֹֽא־יְבַקֵּ֔שׁ וְהַנִּשְׁבֶּ֖רֶת לֹ֣א יְרַפֵּ֑א הַנִּצָּבָה֙ לֹ֣א יְכַלְכֵּ֔ל וּבְשַׂ֤ר הַבְּרִיאָה֙ יֹאכַ֔ל וּפַרְסֵיהֶ֖ן יְפָרֵֽק׃ ס
Woe to[^19] my worthless shepherd, who abandons the flock! May the sword strike his arm and his right eye! May his arm wither completely, and his right eye go totally blind!"
ה֣וֹי רֹעִ֤י הֽ͏ָאֱלִיל֙ עֹזְבִ֣י הַצֹּ֔אן חֶ֥רֶב עַל־זְרוֹע֖וֹ וְעַל־עֵ֣ין יְמִינ֑וֹ זְרֹעוֹ֙ יָב֣וֹשׁ תִּיבָ֔שׁ וְעֵ֥ין יְמִינ֖וֹ כָּהֹ֥ה תִכְהֶֽה׃ ס

n.1: The Hebrew text is written *batsur*, "inaccessible", but read *batsir*, a word that usually means "grape harvest". Both are probably meant to describe a thick forest.
n.2: Hebrew *adderet*, "glory", also the word for a rich robe. Perhaps their rich pastures are meant.
n.3: Literally "the pride of the Jordan", the thick growth along the river where lions lived (Jeremiah 12:5; 49:19).
n.4: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.5: Literally "the flock of slaughter". Also in verse 7. The meaning of verses 4–17 is much debated. The prophet acts out the part of a shepherd, but who the shepherds and the flock stand for is uncertain.
n.6: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement.
n.7: The same consonants can be read "to his shepherd".
n.8: Literally "therefore the afflicted of the flock". The same letters, divided into words differently, can be read "for the sheep traders", and the Septuagint reads it in this way, as a reference to Canaan or Canaanites (traders). Also in verse 11.
n.9: Hebrew *No'am*, "pleasantness, favor", and *Chovelim*, "bonds", that is, the bonds that join Judah and Israel (verse 14).
n.10: The three shepherds have never been identified with certainty.
n.13: Literally "thirty of silver", probably thirty shekels, about 12 ounces (345 grams) of silver: the price paid for a slave who had been gored to death (Exodus 21:32). Matthew 26:15 and 27:3–10 tell how Judas was paid thirty pieces of silver and the money was used to buy a potter's field. Matthew 27:9–10 quotes verses 12–13 as spoken by "Jeremiah the prophet", combining them with words from Jeremiah (compare Jeremiah 18:2–3; 32:6–9).
n.14: Hebrew *ha-yotser*, "the potter". Also later in the verse. The Syriac reads "the treasury" (*ha-otsar*), a word that differs by one letter.
n.15: Spoken with scorn. Literally "the glory of the price at which I was valued by them".
n.16: Hebrew *evili*, "foolish", a word for one who is morally worthless.
n.17: Hebrew *ha-na'ar*, "the youth". Or "the scattered", with a small change to the Hebrew. Compare the bad shepherds of Ezekiel 34:2–4.
n.18: Perhaps by driving the sheep over rough ground, or by tearing the carcass apart to eat it.
n.19: Hebrew *hoy*, here the cry "Woe to" (see 2:10). *Worthless* is Hebrew *ha-elil*, a word often used of idols.

v: An oracle.[^1] The word of the LORD[^2] concerning Israel. Declares the LORD,[^3] who stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the human spirit within a person:
מַשָּׂ֥א דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה נֹטֶ֤ה שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ וְיֹסֵ֣ד אָ֔רֶץ וְיֹצֵ֥ר רֽוּחַ־אָדָ֖ם בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃ פ
Look, I am going to make Jerusalem a cup that makes all the surrounding peoples reel.[^4] Judah too will be under siege, as Jerusalem is.[^5]
הִנֵּ֣ה אָ֠נֹכִי שָׂ֣ם אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלַ֧͏ִם סַף־רַ֛עַל לְכָל־הָעַמִּ֖ים סָבִ֑יב וְגַ֧ם עַל־יְהוּדָ֛ה יִֽהְיֶ֥ה בַמָּצ֖וֹר עַל־יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃
On that day I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone for all the peoples. All who lift it will be badly injured, and all the nations of the earth will gather against her.
וְהָיָ֣ה בַיּוֹם־הַ֠הוּא אָשִׂ֨ים אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֜ם אֶ֤בֶן מַֽעֲמָסָה֙ לְכָל־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים כָּל־עֹמְסֶ֖יהָ שָׂר֣וֹט יִשָּׂרֵ֑טוּ וְנֶאֶסְפ֣וּ עָלֶ֔יהָ כֹּ֖ל גּוֹיֵ֥י הָאָֽרֶץ׃

On that day, declares the LORD, I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness.[^6] But I will keep my eyes open over the house of Judah, when I strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.
בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֗ה אַכֶּ֤ה כָל־סוּס֙ בַּתִּמָּה֔וֹן וְרֹכְב֖וֹ בַּשִּׁגָּע֑וֹן וְעַל־בֵּ֤ית יְהוּדָה֙ אֶפְקַ֣ח אֶת־עֵינַ֔י וְכֹל֙ ס֣וּס הָֽעַמִּ֔ים אַכֶּ֖ה בַּֽעִוָּרֽוֹן׃
Then the clans[^7] of Judah will say in their hearts, "The people who live in Jerusalem are our strength, through the LORD of Armies,[^8] their God."
וְאָֽ[m]מְר֛וּ אַלֻּפֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּלִבָּ֑ם אַמְצָ֥ה לִי֙ יֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם בַּיהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵיהֶֽם׃

On that day I will make the clans of Judah like a fire pot in a pile of wood, like a flaming torch among sheaves. They will devour all the surrounding peoples, right and left, while Jerusalem will remain in its place, in Jerusalem.[^9]

בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא אָשִׂים֩ אֶת־אַלֻּפֵ֨י יְהוּדָ֜ה כְּֽכִיּ֧וֹר אֵ֣שׁ בְּעֵצִ֗ים וּכְלַפִּ֥יד אֵשׁ֙ בְּעָמִ֔יר וְאָ֨כְל֜וּ עַל־יָמִ֧ין וְעַל־שְׂמֹ֛אול אֶת־כָּל־הָעַמִּ֖ים סָבִ֑יב וְיָשְׁבָ֨ה יְרוּשָׁלַ֥͏ִם ע֛וֹד תַּחְתֶּ֖יהָ בִּירוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃ פ
The LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem will not be raised above Judah.
וְהוֹשִׁ֧יעַ יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־אָהֳלֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה בָּרִֽאשֹׁנָ֑ה לְמַ֨עַן לֹֽא־תִגְדַּ֜ל תִּפְאֶ֣רֶת בֵּית־דָּוִ֗יד וְתִפְאֶ֛רֶת יֹשֵׁ֥ב יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם עַל־יְהוּדָֽה׃

On that day the LORD will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the feeblest among them on that day will be like David, and the house of David will be like God,[^10] like the angel of the LORD going before them.
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יָגֵ֤ן יְהוָה֙ בְּעַד֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְהָיָ֞ה הַנִּכְשָׁ֥ל בָּהֶ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא כְּדָוִ֑יד וּבֵ֤ית דָּוִיד֙ כֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים כְּמַלְאַ֥ךְ יְהוָ֖ה לִפְנֵיהֶֽם׃
On that day I will set out to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.
וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא אֲבַקֵּ֗שׁ לְהַשְׁמִיד֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַבָּאִ֖ים עַל־יְרוּשָׁלָֽ͏ִם׃

I will pour out on the house of David and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and of pleading.[^11] They will look on me, the one they have pierced,[^12] and they will mourn for him as one mourns for an only child, and weep bitterly over him as one weeps over a firstborn.

וְשָׁפַכְתִּי֩ עַל־בֵּ֨ית דָּוִ֜יד וְעַ֣ל ׀ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב יְרוּשָׁלִַ֗ם ר֤וּחַ חֵן֙ וְתַ֣חֲנוּנִ֔ים וְהִבִּ֥יטוּ אֵלַ֖י אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־דָּקָ֑רוּ וְסָפְד֣וּ עָלָ֗יו כְּמִסְפֵּד֙ עַל־הַיָּחִ֔יד וְהָמֵ֥ר עָלָ֖יו כְּהָמֵ֥ר עַֽל־הַבְּכֽוֹר׃
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be as great as the mourning for Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.[^13]
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִגְדַּ֤ל הַמִּסְפֵּד֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם כְּמִסְפַּ֥ד הֲדַדְ־רִמּ֖וֹן בְּבִקְעַ֥ת מְגִדּֽוֹן׃
The land will mourn, each clan by itself: the clan of the house of David by itself and their wives by themselves; the clan of the house of Nathan[^14] by itself and their wives by themselves;
וְסָפְדָ֣ה הָאָ֔רֶץ מִשְׁפָּח֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּח֖וֹת לְבָ֑ד מִשְׁפַּ֨חַת בֵּית־דָּוִ֤יד לְבָד֙ וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֣ם לְבָ֔ד מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת בֵּית־נָתָן֙ לְבָ֔ד וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם לְבָֽד׃
the clan of the house of Levi by itself and their wives by themselves; the clan of the Shimeites[^15] by itself and their wives by themselves;
מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת בֵּית־לֵוִי֙ לְבָ֔ד וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם לְבָ֑ד מִשְׁפַּ֤חַת הַשִּׁמְעִי֙ לְבָ֔ד וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם לְבָֽד׃
and all the clans that are left, each clan by itself and their wives by themselves.
כֹּ֗ל הַמִּשְׁפָּחוֹת֙ הַנִּשְׁאָר֔וֹת מִשְׁפָּחֹ֥ת מִשְׁפָּחֹ֖ת לְבָ֑ד וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם לְבָֽד׃ ס

n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.3: Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. Also in verse 4.
n.4: Literally "a basin of reeling". Compare the cup of the LORD's anger in Isaiah 51:17, 22.
n.5: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "and also against Judah it will be in the siege against Jerusalem".
n.6: Panic, madness and blindness are the three curses of Deuteronomy 28:28.
n.7: Hebrew *allufim*, clans or clan chiefs (9:7). Also in verse 6.
n.8: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel.
n.9: Literally "Jerusalem will again dwell in its place, in Jerusalem".
n.11: Hebrew *ruach*, "spirit, wind, breath". *Grace and pleading* may mean a spirit that receives favor and prays for it.
n.12: Literally "They will look to me, whom they have pierced". The Hebrew then changes to "him". Some Hebrew manuscripts read "to him". The Septuagint reads "They will look to me, because they danced in triumph", reading a Hebrew word that differs by one letter. John 19:37 quotes this line as "They will look on the one whom they have pierced", of the death of Jesus, and Revelation 1:7 echoes it.
n.13: Perhaps the mourning for King Josiah, who was killed at Megiddo (2 Kings 23:29–30; 2 Chronicles 35:22–25), if Hadad-rimmon is a place nearby. Or Hadad-rimmon may be a storm god whose death was mourned each year.
n.14: A son of David (2 Samuel 5:14; Luke 3:31).
n.15: Shimei was a grandson of Levi (Numbers 3:17–18, 21).

v: On that day a fountain will be opened for the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and impurity.[^1]
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ מָק֣וֹר נִפְתָּ֔ח לְבֵ֥ית דָּוִ֖יד וּלְיֹשְׁבֵ֣י יְרֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם לְחַטַּ֖את וּלְנִדָּֽה׃

On that day, declares the LORD of Armies,[^2] I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they will be remembered no more. I will also remove from the land the prophets and the spirit of impurity.

וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא נְאֻ֣ם ׀ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת אַכְרִ֞ית אֶת־שְׁמ֤וֹת הָֽעֲצַבִּים֙ מִן־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְלֹ֥א יִזָּכְר֖וּ ע֑וֹד וְגַ֧ם אֶת־הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים וְאֶת־ר֥וּחַ הַטֻּמְאָ֖ה אַעֲבִ֥יר מִן־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

If anyone still prophesies, his father and mother who bore him will say to him, "You will not live, for you have spoken lies in the name of the LORD." And his father and mother who bore him will pierce him[^3] when he prophesies.

וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־יִנָּבֵ֣א אִישׁ֮ עוֹד֒ וְאָמְר֣וּ אֵ֠לָיו אָבִ֨יו וְאִמּ֤וֹ יֹֽלְדָיו֙ לֹ֣א תִֽחְיֶ֔ה כִּ֛י שֶׁ֥קֶר דִּבַּ֖רְתָּ בְּשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֑ה וּדְקָרֻ֜הוּ אָבִ֧יהוּ וְאִמּ֛וֹ יֹלְדָ֖יו בְּהִנָּבְאֽוֹ׃
On that day every prophet will be ashamed of his vision when he prophesies. He will not put on a hairy cloak[^4] in order to deceive.
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יֵבֹ֧שׁוּ הַנְּבִיאִ֛ים אִ֥ישׁ מֵחֶזְיֹנ֖וֹ בְּהִנָּֽבְאֹת֑וֹ וְלֹ֧א יִלְבְּשׁ֛וּ אַדֶּ֥רֶת שֵׂעָ֖ר לְמַ֥עַן כַּחֵֽשׁ׃
He will say, "I am not a prophet. I am a man who works the soil, for the land has been my livelihood since my youth."[^5]
וְאָמַ֕ר לֹ֥א נָבִ֖יא אָנֹ֑כִי אִישׁ־עֹבֵ֤ד אֲדָמָה֙ אָנֹ֔כִי כִּ֥י אָדָ֖ם הִקְנַ֥נִי מִנְּעוּרָֽי׃
And if someone asks him, "What are these wounds on your chest?"[^6] he will say, "I was wounded in the house of my friends."[^7]
וְאָמַ֣ר אֵלָ֔יו מָ֧ה הַמַּכּ֛וֹת הָאֵ֖לֶּה בֵּ֣ין יָדֶ֑יךָ וְאָמַ֕ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֻכֵּ֖יתִי בֵּ֥ית מְאַהֲבָֽי׃ ס

Awake, sword, against my shepherd, against the man who stands next to me,[^8] declares the LORD of Armies. Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered,[^9] and I will turn my hand against the little ones.
חֶ֗רֶב עוּרִ֤י עַל־רֹעִי֙ וְעַל־גֶּ֣בֶר עֲמִיתִ֔י נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת הַ֤ךְ אֶת־הָֽרֹעֶה֙ וּתְפוּצֶ֣יןָ הַצֹּ֔אן וַהֲשִׁבֹתִ֥י יָדִ֖י עַל־הַצֹּעֲרִֽים׃
In the whole land, declares the LORD, two thirds will be cut off and die, and a third will be left in it.
וְהָיָ֤ה בְכָל־הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה פִּֽי־שְׁנַ֣יִם בָּ֔הּ יִכָּרְת֖וּ יִגְוָ֑עוּ וְהַשְּׁלִשִׁ֖ית יִוָּ֥תֶר בָּֽהּ׃

I will bring this third into the fire. I will refine them as silver is refined and test them as gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will answer them. I will say, "They are my people," and they will say, "The LORD is my God."[^10]

וְהֵבֵאתִ֤י אֶת־הַשְּׁלִשִׁית֙ בָּאֵ֔שׁ וּצְרַפְתִּים֙ כִּצְרֹ֣ף אֶת־הַכֶּ֔סֶף וּבְחַנְתִּ֖ים כִּבְחֹ֣ן אֶת־הַזָּהָ֑ב ה֣וּא ׀ יִקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֗י וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֶעֱנֶ֣ה אֹת֔וֹ אָמַ֙רְתִּי֙ עַמִּ֣י ה֔וּא וְה֥וּא יֹאמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽי׃ ס

n.1: Hebrew *niddah*, the impurity of menstruation, and the word used for the water that cleansed from impurity (Numbers 19:9).
n.2: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles. *The LORD of Armies* (Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*) is traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. *Declares the LORD* is Hebrew *ne'um YHWH*, "the declaration of the LORD", a formula that marks a prophet's words as the LORD's own solemn statement. Also in verses 7 and 8.
n.3: The same verb, *daqar*, as *pierced* in 12:10. The law required a false prophet to be put to death, even by his own family (Deuteronomy 13:7–12, 13:6–11 in most English Bibles; 18:20).
n.4: The garment worn by prophets such as Elijah (2 Kings 1:8; 2:13).
n.5: The Hebrew is pointed *adam hiqnani*, "a man sold me" or "a man made me his servant". The same letters, divided into words differently, can be read *adamah qinyani*, "the land has been my livelihood". Compare Amos 7:14.
n.6: Literally "between your hands", that is, on the chest or the back. Prophets of other gods sometimes cut themselves (1 Kings 18:28).
n.8: Literally "against the man who is my companion".
n.9: Jesus quotes these words in Mark 14:27 and Matthew 26:31, of himself and his disciples, in the form "I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered."
n.10: Compare Hosea 2:25 (2:23 in most English Bibles).

v: Look, a day is coming for the LORD,[^1] when the plunder taken from you[^2] will be divided in your midst.
הִנֵּ֥ה יֽוֹם־בָּ֖א לַֽיהוָ֑ה וְחֻלַּ֥ק שְׁלָלֵ֖ךְ בְּקִרְבֵּֽךְ׃

For I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for battle. The city will be captured, the houses plundered and the women raped.[^3] Half of the city will go into exile, but the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.

וְאָסַפְתִּ֨י אֶת־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֥ם ׀ אֶֽל־יְרוּשָׁלִַם֮ לַמִּלְחָמָה֒ וְנִלְכְּדָ֣ה הָעִ֗יר וְנָשַׁ֙סּוּ֙ הַבָּ֣תִּ֔ים וְהַנָּשִׁ֖ים *תשגלנה **תִּשָּׁכַ֑בְנָה וְיָצָ֞א חֲצִ֤י הָעִיר֙ בַּגּוֹלָ֔ה וְיֶ֣תֶר הָעָ֔ם לֹ֥א יִכָּרֵ֖ת מִן־הָעִֽיר׃
Then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations, as he fights on a day of battle.
וְיָצָ֣א יְהוָ֔ה וְנִלְחַ֖ם בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם הָהֵ֑ם כְּי֥וֹם הִֽלָּחֲמ֖ו בְּי֥וֹם קְרָֽב׃

On that day his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives,[^4] which lies east of Jerusalem, and the Mount of Olives will be split in two from east to west by a very wide valley. Half of the mountain will move north, and half of it south.

וְעָמְד֣וּ רַגְלָ֣יו בַּיּוֹם־הַ֠הוּא עַל־הַ֨ר הַזֵּתִ֜ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר עַל־פְּנֵ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִַם֮ מִקֶּדֶם֒ וְנִבְקַע֩ הַ֨ר הַזֵּיתִ֤ים מֵֽחֶצְיוֹ֙ מִזְרָ֣חָה וָיָ֔מָּה גֵּ֖יא גְּדוֹלָ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד וּמָ֨שׁ חֲצִ֥י הָהָ֛ר צָפ֖וֹנָה וְחֶצְיוֹ־נֶֽגְבָּה׃

You will flee by the valley of my mountains,[^5] for the valley of the mountains will reach as far as Azel.[^6] You will flee as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah.[^7] Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with him.[^8]
