וְנַסְתֶּ֣ם גֵּֽיא־הָרַ֗י כִּֽי־יַגִּ֣יעַ גֵּי־הָרִים֮ אֶל־אָצַל֒ וְנַסְתֶּ֗ם כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר נַסְתֶּם֙ מִפְּנֵ֣י הָרַ֔עַשׁ בִּימֵ֖י עֻזִּיָּ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֑ה וּבָא֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהַ֔י כָּל־קְדֹשִׁ֖ים עִמָּֽךְ׃
On that day there will be no light, neither brightness nor frost.[^9]
וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא לֹֽא־יִהְיֶ֣ה א֔וֹר יְקָר֖וֹת *יקפאון **וְקִפָּאֽוֹן׃
It will be one unbroken day,[^10] known to the LORD, neither day nor night, and at evening time there will be light.
וְהָיָ֣ה יוֹם־אֶחָ֗ד ה֛וּא יִוָּדַ֥ע לַֽיהוָ֖ה לֹא־י֣וֹם וְלֹא־לָ֑יְלָה וְהָיָ֥ה לְעֵֽת־עֶ֖רֶב יִֽהְיֶה־אֽוֹר׃
On that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem, half of it to the eastern sea and half of it to the western sea.[^11] It will flow in summer and in winter.
וְהָיָ֣ה ׀ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יֵצְא֤וּ מַֽיִם־חַיִּים֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם חֶצְיָ֗ם אֶל־הַיָּם֙ הַקַּדְמוֹנִ֔י וְחֶצְיָ֖ם אֶל־הַיָּ֣ם הָאַחֲר֑וֹן בַּקַּ֥יִץ וּבָחֹ֖רֶף יִֽהְיֶֽה׃
The LORD will be king over all the earth. On that day the LORD will be one, and his name one.[^12]
וְהָיָ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־כָּל־הָאָ֑רֶץ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִהְיֶ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה אֶחָ֖ד וּשְׁמ֥וֹ אֶחָֽד׃

The whole land will be changed into a plain like the Arabah,[^13] from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem.[^14] But Jerusalem will be raised up and will remain in its place, from the Benjamin Gate to the place of the First Gate and to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.[^15]

יִסּ֨וֹב כָּל־הָאָ֤רֶץ כָּעֲרָבָה֙ מִגֶּ֣בַע לְרִמּ֔וֹן נֶ֖גֶב יְרֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְֽרָאֲמָה֩ וְיָשְׁבָ֨ה תַחְתֶּ֜יהָ לְמִשַּׁ֣עַר בִּנְיָמִ֗ן עַד־מְק֞וֹם שַׁ֤עַר הָֽרִאשׁוֹן֙ עַד־שַׁ֣עַר הַפִּנִּ֔ים וּמִגְדַּ֣ל חֲנַנְאֵ֔ל עַ֖ד יִקְבֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
People will live in it, and there will never again be a curse of destruction.[^16] Jerusalem will live in security.
וְיָ֣שְׁבוּ בָ֔הּ וְחֵ֖רֶם לֹ֣א יִֽהְיֶה־ע֑וֹד וְיָשְׁבָ֥ה יְרוּשָׁלַ֖͏ִם לָבֶֽטַח׃

This will be the plague with which the LORD will strike all the peoples who have made war on Jerusalem: their flesh will rot while they are still standing on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.

וְזֹ֣את ׀ תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה הַמַּגֵּפָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִגֹּ֤ף יְהוָה֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר צָבְא֖וּ עַל־יְרוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם הָמֵ֣ק ׀ בְּשָׂר֗וֹ וְהוּא֙ עֹמֵ֣ד עַל־רַגְלָ֔יו וְעֵינָיו֙ תִּמַּ֣קְנָה בְחֹֽרֵיהֶ֔ן וּלְשׁוֹנ֖וֹ תִּמַּ֥ק בְּפִיהֶֽם׃
On that day a great panic from the LORD will fall on them. Each will seize the hand of his neighbor, and they will raise their hands against each other.
וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא תִּֽהְיֶ֧ה מְהֽוּמַת־יְהוָ֛ה רַבָּ֖ה בָּהֶ֑ם וְהֶחֱזִ֗יקוּ אִ֚ישׁ יַ֣ד רֵעֵ֔הוּ וְעָלְתָ֥ה יָד֖וֹ עַל־יַ֥ד רֵעֵֽהוּ׃
Judah too will fight at Jerusalem.[^17] The wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered: gold, silver and clothing in great abundance.
וְגַ֨ם־יְהוּדָ֔ה תִּלָּחֵ֖ם בִּירֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְאֻסַּף֩ חֵ֨יל כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֜ם סָבִ֗יב זָהָ֥ב וָכֶ֛סֶף וּבְגָדִ֖ים לָרֹ֥ב מְאֹֽד׃
A plague like this will also strike the horses, the mules, the camels, the donkeys and all the animals in those camps.
וְכֵ֨ן תִּֽהְיֶ֜ה מַגֵּפַ֣ת הַסּ֗וּס הַפֶּ֙רֶד֙ הַגָּמָ֣ל וְהַחֲמ֔וֹר וְכָ֨ל־הַבְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִהְיֶ֖ה בַּמַּחֲנ֣וֹת הָהֵ֑מָּה כַּמַּגֵּפָ֖ה הַזֹּֽאת׃
Then all who are left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the LORD of Armies,[^18] and to celebrate the Festival of Booths.[^19]
וְהָיָ֗ה כָּל־הַנּוֹתָר֙ מִכָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם הַבָּאִ֖ים עַל־יְרֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם וְעָל֞וּ מִדֵּ֧י שָׁנָ֣ה בְשָׁנָ֗ה לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺת֙ לְמֶ֙לֶךְ֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וְלָחֹ֖ג אֶת־חַ֥ג הַסֻּכּֽוֹת׃
If any of the clans of the earth do not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of Armies, there will be no rain on them.
וְ֠הָיָה אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יַעֲלֶ֜ה מֵאֵ֨ת מִשְׁפְּח֤וֹת הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ אֶל־יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם לְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֔ת לְמֶ֖לֶךְ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וְלֹ֥א עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יִהְיֶ֥ה הַגָּֽשֶׁם׃
If the clan of Egypt does not go up and come in, they will have no rain.[^20] There will be the plague with which the LORD strikes the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
וְאִם־מִשְׁפַּ֨חַת מִצְרַ֧יִם לֹֽא־תַעֲלֶ֛ה וְלֹ֥א בָאָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה הַמַּגֵּפָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִגֹּ֤ף יְהוָה֙ אֶת־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יַֽעֲל֔וּ לָחֹ֖ג אֶת־חַ֥ג הַסֻּכּֽוֹת׃
This will be the punishment[^21] of Egypt and the punishment of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
זֹ֥את תִּהְיֶ֖ה חַטַּ֣את מִצְרָ֑יִם וְחַטַּאת֙ כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יַֽעֲל֔וּ לָחֹ֖ג אֶת־חַ֥ג הַסֻּכּֽוֹת׃
On that day the bells of the horses will bear the words "Holy to the LORD",[^22] and the cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the sprinkling bowls in front of the altar.
בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא יִֽהְיֶה֙ עַל־מְצִלּ֣וֹת הַסּ֔וּס קֹ֖דֶשׁ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וְהָיָ֤ה הַסִּירוֹת֙ בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה כַּמִּזְרָקִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֥י הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

Every cooking pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be holy to the LORD of Armies, and all who offer sacrifices will come and take some of them and cook in them. And on that day there will no longer be a trader[^23] in the house of the LORD of Armies.

וְ֠הָיָה כָּל־סִ֨יר בִּירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם וּבִֽיהוּדָ֗ה קֹ֚דֶשׁ לַיהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת וּבָ֙אוּ֙ כָּל־הַזֹּ֣בְחִ֔ים וְלָקְח֥וּ מֵהֶ֖ם וּבִשְּׁל֣וּ בָהֶ֑ם וְלֹא־יִהְיֶ֨ה כְנַעֲנִ֥י ע֛וֹד בְּבֵית־יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃

n.1: *LORD*: God's personal name, Hebrew YHWH, written "the LORD" in capitals as in most English Bibles.
n.2: Literally "your plunder". The Hebrew is feminine, addressing Jerusalem.
n.3: The Hebrew text is written with a coarse word for sexual violation but read with a milder one, "lain with".
n.4: The ridge east of Jerusalem, across the Kidron Valley. Only here in the Old Testament is it called by this name (compare 2 Samuel 15:30; Acts 1:11–12).
n.5: The same consonants can be read "The valley of my mountains will be blocked", as the Septuagint reads. Also later in the verse.
n.7: The earthquake in the eighth century BC, which Amos 1:1 also mentions.
n.8: Hebrew "with you". The Septuagint, the Syriac and the Vulgate read "with him". The holy ones are the angels of the LORD's heavenly army (Deuteronomy 33:2–3; Psalm 89:6, 89:5 in most English Bibles). Compare 1 Thessalonians 3:13.
n.9: The Hebrew is difficult. Literally "there will be no light, precious things and congealing". The Hebrew text is written "the precious things will congeal". The Septuagint reads "there will be no light, and cold and frost".
n.10: Literally "one day", perhaps a day like no other (compare Genesis 1:5).
n.11: The Dead Sea and the Mediterranean. Compare Ezekiel 47:1–12; Joel 4:18 (3:18 in most English Bibles).
n.12: Compare Deuteronomy 6:4. This verse ends the *Aleinu* prayer of Jewish daily worship.
n.13: The deep valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea.
n.14: Geba was at the northern border of Judah (2 Kings 23:8), and Rimmon in the south (Joshua 15:32).
n.15: The gates and the tower were landmarks at the edges of the city (Jeremiah 31:38; 37:13; Nehemiah 3:1).
n.16: Hebrew *cherem*, the ban by which a city was devoted to destruction (Joshua 6:17). Compare Revelation 22:3.
n.18: Hebrew *YHWH tseva'ot*, traditionally "the LORD of hosts" or "the LORD Almighty". *Tseva'ot* means armies: the heavenly hosts and the armies of Israel. Also in verses 17 and 21.
n.19: The autumn festival at the end of the harvest, when the people lived in booths (Leviticus 23:33–43). It came just before the rainy season.
n.20: Literally "and not on them". *Rain* is supplied from verse 17. Egypt depends on the Nile rather than on rain. The Septuagint and the Syriac do not have "not": "on them will come the plague".
n.21: Hebrew *chatta't*, "sin", here the punishment for sin.
n.22: The words engraved on the gold plate on the high priest's turban (Exodus 28:36).
n.23: Literally "a Canaanite", a word also used for a merchant (Zephaniah 1:11; Proverbs 31:24). Compare John 2:16.
